entries.source:
A guard met them at the gate.
	By the color of his skin and the musical way he spoke, the man seemed to have a Tsurani background, though it was also possible he was originally Keshian by nationality. Staring at them dispassionately, he barred their way.
	"No entry," the guard said, shaking his head. "You may come back at daybreak."
	"We were just looking to..."
	"No entry," the guard replied. "No exceptions..."�
entries.translation:
一名守衛在門口攔住了他們。
	從他的膚色與說話時那種帶著音律感的腔調看來，這男人似乎有圖蘭尼血統，不過他也可能原本就是凱許人。他面無表情地盯著他們，擋住了去路。
	「不准進去，」守衛搖著頭說。「你們可以天亮後再回來。」
	「我們只是想……」
	「不准進去，」守衛回答道。「沒有例外……」�

entries.source:
The heavy, metal gate greeted their arrival.
	When they were, at last, allowed entry to the garrison, they were lead back to a meeting with Captain Belford. Pleasantries were exchanged as the men shook hands.
	"You and your men have done a good job in this area, Captain," said @4. "It's no longer under martial law, I see."
	Belford sat a little straighter in his chair, "Thank-you. I've had patrols out rounding up every pointy-eared bast --" he caught himself, remembering Gorath was in the room.  "--well, we've captured a number of moredhel prisoners, the last group of which had some large dogs with them. We didn't have food to keep them and they seemed harmless, so we turned them out..."
	"Trained beasthounds, no doubt," sighed @4. "Probably out looking for ñusð!"
	They thanked Captain Belford for his information, then left.�
entries.translation:
沉重的鐵門迎接了他們的到來。
	當他們終於獲准進入駐防要塞後，便被領去與貝爾福德隊長會面。兩人握手寒暄了一番。
	「隊長，你跟你的手下把這一帶治理得很好，」@4說。「我看，這裡已經不再實施戒嚴了。」
	貝爾福德在椅子上坐得挺直了些，「謝謝誇獎。我派了不少巡邏隊出去，抓了不少那些尖耳朵的混——」他突然打住，想起戈拉斯也在場。「——呃，總之，我們抓到了不少莫瑞德人囚犯，最後一批身邊還帶著幾隻大狗。我們沒有多餘的糧食養牠們，牠們看起來也不會傷人，所以就把牠們放了……」
	「毫無疑問是訓練有素的獵魔犬，」@4嘆了口氣。「大概正在外頭找ñ我們ð呢！」
	他們謝過貝爾福德隊長提供的情報，隨後離開了。�

entries.source:
The Garrison was impressive.
	Sitting high on a hill overlooking LaMut, the military outpost had been constructed years earlier to head off a possible moredhel assault on the western border of the kingdom.
	They followed a road that snaked through town and up the rocky hill upon which the garrison sat. After speaking with the sentries at the gate, they were lead under the fortress's massive iron portcullis.�
entries.translation:
這座駐防要塞令人印象深刻。
	這座軍事哨站坐落在俯瞰拉姆特的山丘高處，多年前建造，目的是為了阻擋莫瑞德人可能對王國西境發動的攻勢。
	他們沿著一條蜿蜒穿過城鎮、爬上要塞所在岩丘的道路前進。與門口的哨兵交談過後，便被領著穿過要塞那扇巨大的鐵閘門。�

entries.source:
Captain Belford stood as they entered the room.
	"It's good to see you once again, @4," he said, extending his hand.
	"I share that sentiment. What news have you? How is Earl Kasumi?" @4 asked as the men shook hands.
	They sat in hard wooden chairs as Belford replied. "He's well, but he's off taking care of some business with a few new guards come through the rift from Kelewan. As for the rest of us, we're looking for a group of grey warriors from Kelewan who slipped through the rift just before it closed."
	@4 looked a little puzzled. "King Lyam and Emperor Ichindar granted the grey warriors freedom and new status in the Kingdom."
	"Yes, but the agreement doesn't allow for the nationalization of stolen goods. Seems they may have absconded with a valuable ruby from Makala's entourage," said Belford.
	"Makala? The Tsurani Great One?" @3 asked.
	Belford smiled. "Yes. He has been talking to Prince Arutha about establishing a permanent rift to encourage trade between the Kingdom and Kelewan. He's really throwing his weight around trying to get his ruby back. If you should happen to come across it, bring it back here -- he's offering a reward!"
	They thanked him for his information and left.�
entries.translation:
貝爾福德隊長見他們進屋便站了起來。
	「很高興能再見到你，@4，」他說著，伸出了手。
	「我也有同感。你有什麼消息？卡蘇米伯爵近況如何？」@4一邊問道，一邊與他握手。
	他們在硬邦邦的木椅上坐下，貝爾福德回答道：「他很好，只是正忙著處理一些事務——有幾名新守衛剛從凱勒旺穿過裂界過來。至於我們其他人，正在找一群灰袍武士，他們是從凱勒旺來的，就在裂界關閉前溜了過來。」
	@4露出有點困惑的神情。「萊亞姆王與伊金達皇帝已經賜予那些灰袍武士自由，讓他們在王國裡有了新的身分。」
	「沒錯，但那份協議並不允許他們把偷來的東西據為己有。看來他們可能從馬卡拉的隨從那裡順走了一顆珍貴的紅寶石，」貝爾福德說。
	「馬卡拉？那位圖蘭尼至尊法師？」@3問道。
	貝爾福德笑了。「沒錯。他一直在跟亞魯莎親王商討，想建立一道永久的裂界，促進王國與凱勒旺之間的貿易往來。他現在為了討回那顆紅寶石可是動用了不少人脈。要是你們碰巧遇上了它，記得帶回這裡來——他開出了懸賞！」
	他們謝過他提供的情報，隨後離開了。�

entries.source:
Captain Belford greeted them with a smile.
	"What brings you back here?" he asked cordially.
	@4 drew out the ruby they had discovered. Holding it out for Bedford to see the gemstone caught a shaft of sunlight, splashing the walls with thousands of twinkling red spots.
	"Are you returning Makala's ruby?" asked Belford.�
entries.translation:
貝爾福德隊長微笑著迎接他們。
	「什麼風把你們吹回來了？」他親切地問道。
	@4取出了他們找到的那顆紅寶石。舉起讓貝爾福德查看，寶石正好接住一道陽光，把牆上灑滿了成千上萬個閃爍的紅色光點。
	「你們是來歸還馬卡拉的紅寶石的嗎？」貝爾福德問道。�

entries.source:
@4 shook his head.
	"I still don't trust the Tsurani," he said. "We're going to hold onto it for a while."
	Belford tried to get him to change his mind, even going so far as to threaten throwing him in jail, but @4 held firm.  At last the tired captain gave up.
	"Okay," he said with a faint trace of laughter in his voice, "You win. If Makala comes back I'll just tell him we couldn't find the blasted thing."�
entries.translation:
@4搖了搖頭。
	「我還是不信任圖蘭尼人，」他說。「我們打算先留著它一陣子。」
	貝爾福德試著讓他改變主意，甚至還揚言要把他關進大牢，但@4依然堅持己見。最後，這位疲憊的隊長終於放棄了。
	「好吧，」他說道，聲音裡帶著一絲隱約的笑意，「算你們贏了。要是馬卡拉回來，我就跟他說我們找不到那該死的東西。」�

entries.source:
@4 smiled.
	"It's good to see you again, Captain Belford," he said, nodding in the direction of the uniformed man approaching them. "What news have you?"
	Belford extended a hand and replied, "We continue to hear reports of trouble brewing in the Northlands, and we've spotted a number of the bloody moredhel bastards around here -- what news have you for ñmeð?"
	They talked for nearly an hour, exchanging stories and information. Finally, all new news exhausted, they shook hands and said good-bye.�
entries.translation:
@4笑了。
	「真高興又見到你了，貝爾福德隊長，」他說著，朝著走近的軍裝男子點了點頭。「你有什麼消息？」
	貝爾福德伸出手回答道：「我們持續收到北境局勢不穩的回報，這附近也發現了不少該死的莫瑞德人混蛋——你們有什麼消息要告訴ñ我ð嗎？」
	他們談了將近一個鐘頭，交換了各自的見聞與情報。最後，新消息都聊完了，兩人握手道別。�

entries.source:
Guards hurried across the courtyard.
	A red-eyed soldier met them at the central keep's door, his wolf's head tabard stained red with streaks of blood and his arm wound in bandages. Scratching his stubbled chin, he asked them what they wanted.
	"What in Tith's hells happened to you?" @4 said, looking the soldier over. "Looks like you were caught in a terrible fight."
	"Moredhel," the man croaked. "Whole clutch of their moss troopers were operating near here and we found them out. We've had to impose martial law until we're sure we've routed them. LaMutian soldiers strung from here all the way to Hawk's Hollow in the south and east all the way to Tyr-Sog."
	"Have any idea what they were up to?" @4 asked.
	"None," the man replied. "Though they all seemed fairly upset about something going on to the south. I'm not exactly sure what."
	@4 nodded and turned to go, but the guard reached through the gate and snagged his sleeve. "Don't be out on the roads at ónight if you can at all help it. Our guards have orders to kill on sight anyone trying to pass through our checkpoints."�
entries.translation:
守衛們匆匆穿過庭院。
	一名雙眼佈滿血絲的士兵在中央主樓的門口迎上他們，他那件繡著狼頭紋章的外衣上沾滿了斑斑血跡，手臂也纏著繃帶。他搔了搔滿是鬍渣的下巴，問他們有何貴幹。
	「提斯神在上，你到底怎麼了？」@4打量著這名士兵說道。「看起來像是被捲進了一場惡戰。」
	「莫瑞德人，」那男人啞著嗓子說。「有一整批他們的沼澤部隊在這附近活動，被我們發現了。在確定已經把他們肅清之前，我們不得不實施戒嚴。從這裡一路到南邊的鷹谷，再到東邊的泰索格，都佈滿了拉姆特的士兵。」
	「知道他們在打什麼主意嗎？」@4問道。
	「不知道，」那男人回答。「不過他們似乎都對南邊發生的某件事相當不安。我也不太清楚是什麼事。」
	@4點了點頭，轉身要走，守衛卻伸手隔著閘門抓住他的袖子。「要是能不出門，就別在ó夜裡在路上走動。我們的守衛接到命令，只要有人試圖闖過我們的檢查哨，一律格殺勿論。」�

entries.source:
A thin little man greeted them at the door.
	"I'm Keifer Alescook. Have you come to buy or sell some gems?" he questioned in a frail voice.
	@4 moved closer to the door. "We're looking for a ruby that may have been stolen by a group of Grey Warriors. Have you purchased any gemstones from such men?"
	"I don't know what you're talking about," the man said quickly. "I don't buy ñstolen merchandise. You might try talking to a fellow I ran into north of Hawk's Hollow about it. Name's Isaac if I recall." The man looked about nervously. "I'm...er...not open for business right now. You'll have to come back later."
	Before @4 could say another word Keifer had closed the door.�

The door opened slightly.
	Peering at them without opening the door all the way, a thin man rubbed the sleep from his eyes. "I'm not open for business right now. You'll have to come back later," he said.
	"Business?" Glancing down the side of the house, @4 looked for a sign or shingle, but none was in evidence. "What do you sell?"
	"I'm a gems dealer---Keifer Alescook---but I don't have anything in stock right now," he said with irritation. "It's likely to be several weeks before I get anything again, so please go away."
	Before @4 could say another word Keifer had closed the door.�
entries.translation:
門微微開了一條縫。
	一個瘦削的男人沒把門完全打開，就這樣窺視著他們，一邊揉著惺忪睡眼。「我現在沒開門營業。你們得晚點再來，」他說。
	「營業？」@4瞥了瞥屋子側邊，想找塊招牌或牌匾，卻什麼也沒看到。「你是賣什麼的？」
	「我是個寶石商——凱佛艾爾庫克——但我現在手頭上什麼存貨都沒有，」他不耐煩地說道。「大概還要好幾個星期才會再進貨，所以請你們離開吧。」
	@4話還沒說完，凱佛就已經把門關上了。�

entries.source: "You've doone it! I 'eard the conflagration down the shaft but I 'ad no idea what was a'happenin'! Congratulations!"�
entries.translation: 「你們成功啦！我在坑道下頭聽到那陣爆炸聲，都不知道到底發生什麼事哩！恭喜恭喜！」�

entries.source: "Right now, I think we all could just use a rest..."�
entries.translation: 「現在啊，我看我們大家都該歇一歇了……」�

entries.source: "A rest you'll have and you'll be a'needin' it! You'll 'ave to 'ave your strength to be carryin' about all the gold in rewards! Well done!"�
entries.translation: 「歇是要歇的，你們也真是該歇歇了！身子骨可得養好，才扛得動那一大堆賞金哪！幹得漂亮！」�

entries.source: The dwarf handed @4 a pouch of gold coins, then disappeared down the damp shaft of the mine.�
entries.translation: 那矮人遞給@4一袋金幣，隨後便消失在礦坑潮濕的坑道裡。�

entries.source:
The face of the door was covered with a pattern; a strange semi-circle formed of oily black smudges that joined at the iron door latch. On closer examination, it seemed that the smudges were actually fingerprints of some kind...
	"I really should have that cleaned, I suppose." @4 jerked upright at the sound of the gruff voice. Padding from around the corner of the house, a balding man stopped next to @0 and held up a palm stained with black ink. "A scribe tends to make quite a mess. Occupational hazard."
	"Scribe?"
	"Among other things," he said. "Currently I have accepted a commission on behalf of a travelling merchant to do a survey of all the mercantile boxes in the area." He cast a knowing look at @5. "Perhaps you would be interested in helping."
	"And what would we profit of it?" @5 said quietly.
	"Information," the scribe replied. "I've acquired a book I think you'll find very interesting. There's a box just west of Hawk's Hollow, on the southern side of a small hill. Find out what's in that box and I'll give you the book. Now leave me. I have much work to do."�
entries.translation:
門板上覆著一層圖案；一個由油膩黑漬構成的詭異半圓形，在鐵門閂處交會。仔細一看，那些黑漬似乎其實是某種指紋……
	「我想我真該把這個清乾淨了。」聽見這粗啞的聲音，@4猛地站直身子。一個微禿的男人從屋角踱步過來，在@0身旁停下，舉起一隻沾滿黑墨的手掌。「當抄寫員總是容易弄得一團糟。職業病嘛。」
	「抄寫員？」
	「還兼做點別的，」他說。「目前我接下了一位行商的委託，要對這一帶所有的商用箱子做個調查。」他意味深長地看了@5一眼。「或許你們會有興趣幫個忙。」
	「那我們能得到什麼好處？」@5輕聲問道。
	「情報，」那抄寫員回答道。「我手上有一本書，我想你們會覺得很有意思。鷹谷正西邊有個箱子，就在一座小山丘的南側。查出那箱子裡裝著什麼，我就把書給你們。現在讓我一個人靜靜吧，我還有很多事要忙。」�

entries.source:
Jeremy answered their knock at the door.
	"Ah, my friends. I see you have returned. What can you tell of the box I asked you about?"
	@4 rubbed a loose floorboard with the tip of his boot. "We don't know."
	"I cannot -- I ñwill not -- give you the book until you tell me the contents of that box. I told you before, it's west of Hawk's Hollow and south of a small hill. Now go."�
entries.translation:
傑瑞米應了他們的敲門聲。
	「啊，我的朋友們。看來你們回來了。那個箱子的事，你們有什麼消息？」
	@4用靴尖蹭著一塊鬆動的地板。「我們不知道。」
	「在你們告訴我箱子裡裝了什麼之前，我不能——我ñ不會——把書給你們。我之前跟你們說過了，就在鷹谷西邊、一座小山丘的南邊。現在走吧。」�

entries.source:
The face of the door was covered with a pattern; a strange semi-circle formed of oily black smudges that joined at the iron door latch. On closer examination, it seemed that the smudges were actually fingerprints of some kind...
	"I really should have that cleaned, I suppose." @4 jerked upright at the sound of the gruff voice. Padding from around the corner of the house, a balding man stopped next to @0 and held up a palm stained with black ink. "A scribe tends to make quite a mess. Occupational hazard."
	"Scribe?"
	"Among other things," he said. "Currently I have accepted a commission on behalf of a travelling merchant to do a survey of all the mercantile boxes in the area. Perhaps you would be interested in helping..."
	"And what would we profit of it?" @4 said quietly.
	"Information," the scribe replied. "I've acquired a book I think you'll find very interesting. There's a box just west of Hawk's Hollow, on the southern side of a small hill. I suspect it has been trapped. Find out for me and I'll give you my book."
	@4 frowned. "As it turns out, we have already ñfound that particular box. It ñwas trapped," he said.
	"Oh! Well, better that you discovered it than me," he said. He walked to a small bookshelf in the corner of his house and drew out a large volume. Returning he handed it to @4.
	"Happy reading. Now, I really must be about my business."�
entries.translation:
門板上覆著一層圖案；一個由油膩黑漬構成的詭異半圓形，在鐵門閂處交會。仔細一看，那些黑漬似乎其實是某種指紋……
	「我想我真該把這個清乾淨了。」聽見這粗啞的聲音，@4猛地站直身子。一個微禿的男人從屋角踱步過來，在@0身旁停下，舉起一隻沾滿黑墨的手掌。「當抄寫員總是容易弄得一團糟。職業病嘛。」
	「抄寫員？」
	「還兼做點別的，」他說。「目前我接下了一位行商的委託，要對這一帶所有的商用箱子做個調查。或許你們會有興趣幫個忙……」
	「那我們能得到什麼好處？」@4輕聲問道。
	「情報，」那抄寫員回答道。「我手上有一本書，我想你們會覺得很有意思。鷹谷正西邊有個箱子，就在一座小山丘的南側。我懷疑那裡頭裝了陷阱。幫我查清楚，我就把書給你們。」
	@4皺起眉頭。「說來也巧，我們ñ已經找到那個箱子了。裡頭ñ確實有陷阱，」他說。
	「哦！好吧，還好是你們發現的，不是我，」他說。他走向屋角一個小書架，抽出一本厚重的書。回來後遞給了@4。
	「祝你們讀得愉快。現在，我真的該去忙我的正事了。」�

entries.source:
"Bring us... armor... Grey Tower Plate..." croaked the Kobold.
	Without another word the creature slipped back into the darkness of the pit.�
entries.translation:
「給我們……鎧甲……灰塔鎧甲……」那科博德啞聲說道。
	話音未落，那怪物便滑回了坑裡的黑暗之中。�

entries.source:
"We would have...Grey Tower Plate," croaked the Kobold. "Have you... of what... we speak?"
	@4 considered the question for a moment, unsure how to answer...�
entries.translation:
「我們想要……灰塔鎧甲，」那科博德啞聲說道。「你們……可知道……我們在說什麼？」
	@4想了一會兒這個問題，不確定該怎麼回答……�

entries.source:
@4 shook his head.
	Considering the trouble they had gone through to get the dwarven armor, he wasn't quite prepared to simply give it away, despite the tempting offer that the kobolds had made. "We haven't found it as yet," he lied. "We will make certain to return it to you if we do find it."�
entries.translation:
@4搖了搖頭。
	想到他們為了拿到這副矮人鎧甲吃了多少苦頭，儘管科博德開出的條件相當誘人，他還是不太願意就這麼白白送出去。「我們還沒找到，」他撒了個謊。「要是找到了，我們一定會送回來給你們的。」�

entries.source:
A shiny stone caught @1's eye.
	Upon closer inspection he realized the stone wasn't actually a stone at all. He had found a piece of metal poking up through the packed dirt. He bent down to take a closer look, tried to brush away the years of dust and dirt and rocks that had swallowed it and now refused to let go.
	Digging with the edge of his sword to free it from its earthen tomb, he found the item was bigger than he originally suspected, but at last it was free.
	He had found an ancient suit of dwarven armor known as Grey Tower Plate!�
entries.translation:
一塊發亮的石頭吸引了@1的目光。
	仔細一看，他發現那根本不是石頭。他找到了一小塊從夯實的泥土裡冒出來的金屬。他蹲下身仔細查看，試著撥開那覆蓋在上頭、多年來累積的塵土與碎石，然而它們卻緊緊不放。
	他用劍緣挖掘，想把它從這座泥土墳墓裡解放出來，這才發現這東西比他原先猜想的還要大，但最終還是把它挖了出來。
	他找到了一套古老的矮人鎧甲，人稱灰塔鎧甲！�

entries.source:
Soldiers halted them.
	Arrayed across the road were a small group of men, all wearing knee-length tabards of white emblazoned with a grey wolf's head on a circle of blue, the well-known colors of the LaMutian Garrison.
	"You are breaking the curfew," one of the guards said coolly. "We have orders to put to ódeath any that are found roaming these roads at night."
	Knowing that an explanation was expected, @4 licked his lips. "Ah, well, we have good reason to be out," he said, scrambling for an excuse that sounded reasonable...�
entries.translation:
士兵們攔下了他們。
	一小群人橫在路上排開，全都穿著白色的及膝外衣，上面繡著藍色圓圈裡的灰狼頭紋章，那是拉姆特駐防要塞眾所皆知的軍徽。
	「你們違反了宵禁，」其中一名守衛冷冷地說道。「我們接到命令，凡是在夜裡發現遊蕩在這些道路上的人，一律ó處死。」
	@4明白對方在等一個解釋，他舔了舔嘴唇。「啊，這個嘛，我們外出是有正當理由的，」他說著，努力想擠出一個聽起來合理的藉口……�

entries.source:
The guards nodded.
	"Very well," one of them said. "Be on your way, but don't let us find you walking after dark again until martial law is lifted."�
entries.translation:
守衛們點了點頭。
	「很好，」其中一人說道。「你們走吧，但在戒嚴解除之前，別再讓我們發現你們天黑後還在外面走動。」�

entries.source:
@4 had made a ómistake.
	Though he wasn't certain what he had said wrong, he had noticed the nearly invisible flicker of a smirk which had appeared on the guards' faces. Patiently, they waited until @4 had finished his bluff.
	"That's a óvery interesting story...,"
	"...Unfortunately it is also very false."�
entries.translation:
@4犯了個ó錯。
	雖然他不確定自己到底說錯了什麼，但他注意到守衛們臉上閃過一絲幾乎難以察覺的竊笑。他們耐著性子，等@4把這番信口胡謅的話講完。
	「這故事真是ó有意思……」
	「……可惜也非常假。」�

entries.source: The leader of the guard looked them in the eyes and said, "I hope you three are good with your weapons."�
entries.translation: 守衛的隊長直視著他們的眼睛，說道：「希望你們三位的武藝過得去。」�

entries.source:
@4 stopped.
	He looked at the band guarding the pass ahead and called out, "Will you allow us safe passage?"
	An answer was returned swiftly and with great authority, "By the order of Prince Arutha, we forbid you to come any further."
	Cupping a hand to his mouth, @4 called back, "We are on official kingdom business. You must let us pass."
	"We have strict orders not to allow anyone further east," came the response.
	@0 stepped forward and stood next to @4. "What shall we do?"
	"We are greatly outnumbered, we should leave."�

@4 strained to hear.
	Standing near the entrance, bits of conversation coming from the table nearby were occasionally managing to fight their way through the other noises in the tavern.
	"...fools from Eggley..." he heard.  Then another man said in a hushed voice, "He was looking for Stellan, something about unpaid debts, but..."
	The voices dipped back beneath the surface of noise and @4 could hear no more.�
entries.translation:
@4努力想聽清楚。
	他站在門口附近，附近桌子傳來的隻言片語不時穿過酒館裡的其他噪音，勉強傳進他耳裡。
	「……艾格利來的一群傻瓜……」他聽見。接著另一個男人壓低了聲音說：「他在找史特倫，說是欠債沒還之類的，不過……」
	那些聲音又沉回了嘈雜聲底下，@4再也聽不清楚了。�

entries.source:
A shifty-eyed man motioned them over.
	"Boys!" he said. "'Snake Eyes' Spitzer's the name. You feeling lucky tonight? You're ñlooking lucky. How about a game of dice?"�
entries.translation:
一個眼神閃爍的男人朝他們招了招手。
	「小夥子們！」他說。「人稱『蛇眼』史比策。今晚手氣如何啊？看你們ñ挺走運的樣子。要不要來局擲骰子？」�

entries.source:
They joined a shifty-eyed man.
	"No games right now, fellas! I owe some money to a bloke in the back room and I don't think he would appreciate me giving it to ñyou in a game of chance."
	Noticing that the man seemed a little nervous, @4 said, "Who is this person you owe money?"
	"He's known by folks around here as 'The Collector'." He lowered his voice until it was barely more than a whisper, "They say he killed a fella over in Eggley called 'Stellan.'"
	"Well, perhaps we can find a game with you on another day," @4 said.�
entries.translation:
他們湊到了那個眼神閃爍的男人身邊。
	「現在不玩了，兄弟們！我欠了後屋一個傢伙一筆錢，我想他大概不會樂意我把錢給ñ你們，拿去賭博。」
	注意到這男人似乎有點緊張，@4問道：「你欠的這個人是誰？」
	「這一帶的人都管他叫『收帳人』。」他把聲音壓得幾乎只剩耳語，「聽說他在艾格利殺過一個叫『史特倫』的傢伙。」
	「好吧，或許改天我們能找你玩一局，」@4說。�

entries.source:
A sleepy man pushed them aside.
	Blinking, but unable to get one eye to completely open, the man stumbled to a bedroll in the corner of the room and laid down.
	"Are you the man known as 'The Collector?'" asked @4.
	He sat up grumpily and finally managing to get both eyes open, responded, "What if I am?"
	"It would appear you have a debt that hasn't been paid you by an acolyte at the Temple of Silban. We just thought you should know."
	A glimmer of...greed appeared in the man's eyes. Suddenly more awake now, he said in a somewhat cheerful voice, "Thank you! I shall pay him a visit on the morrow!"�
entries.translation:
一個睡眼惺忪的男人把他們推到一旁。
	他眨著眼睛，卻怎麼也睜不開一隻眼，跌跌撞撞地走到房間角落的一張鋪蓋上躺下。
	「你就是人稱『收帳人』的那個人嗎？」@4問道。
	他沒好氣地坐起身，終於把兩隻眼睛都睜開，回道：「就算是又怎樣？」
	「看來席爾班神殿有個見習修士欠了你一筆債沒還。我們只是覺得你該知道這事。」
	那男人的眼裡閃過一絲……貪婪的光芒。他頓時清醒了不少，用略帶愉快的語氣說：「多謝你們！我明天就去拜訪拜訪他！」�

entries.source:
A sleepy man glared at them.
	@4 couldn't help but feel the man was sizing them up in some way, but he seemed harmless enough so they thought nothing else of it.�
entries.translation:
一個睡眼惺忪的男人瞪著他們。
	@4總覺得這男人似乎在暗自打量他們，但對方看起來也沒什麼惡意，於是他們也就不再多想。�

entries.source:
Something shiny caught @0's eye.
	Bending down to take a closer look he brushed aside several layers of dirt and scrub brush to reveal a badly damaged suit of Elven armor! Pulling on the suit to remove it from the ground he was surprised at the ease with which he was able to free it. It had obviously been buried by something ñother than the years.�
entries.translation:
一件閃亮的東西吸引了@0的目光。
	他彎下腰仔細一看，撥開了好幾層泥土與灌木叢，赫然露出一套嚴重損毀的精靈鎧甲！他拉扯著想把它從地裡拔出來，卻驚訝地發現竟然毫不費力就拔了出來。顯然，把它埋起來的並非只是ñ歲月而已。�

entries.source: "Strange. These tracks near the armor I found appear to be elven, judging by the patterns of their footwear in the dirt."�
entries.translation: 「奇怪。從腳印的形狀判斷，我找到的這副鎧甲附近的足跡，看起來像是精靈的。」�

entries.source: "What is strange? Elves travel these roads frequently, I would imagine."�
entries.translation: 「奇怪在哪？我猜精靈常常走這些路吧。」�

entries.source: "What I find puzzling is that a band appears to have travelled this way from Eggley. But right over there you can see they stopped for a while, then skirted to the west of the road back toward town."�
entries.translation: 「讓我覺得奇怪的是，似乎有一隊人是從艾格利那個方向走過來的。但你看那邊，他們在那裡停了一陣子，然後又繞到路的西側，往鎮上折返回去了。」�

entries.source:
@0 disappeared.
	Turning, @1 found him on one knee, his hand wiping gently at something in the dirt...�
entries.translation:
@0不見了。
	轉過身，@1發現他單膝跪地，正輕輕擦拭著泥土裡的某樣東西……�

entries.source:
"These tracks appear to be elven. I'd say a band of them passed through here not long ago."
	"Strange. It appears they left Eggley, stopped for a while here and then headed east towards town again, as though they were looping back."�
entries.translation:
「這些腳印看起來像是精靈的。我猜有一隊精靈不久前經過這裡。」
	「奇怪。看來他們是從艾格利出來的，在這裡停了一陣子，然後又往東朝鎮上走回去，像是繞了一圈折返似的。」�

entries.source:
The man didn't look happy.
	"He don't talk much," called a voice from the other side of the tavern. "He's a pretty somber fellow. Folks call him Grimm 'cuz he never laughs or smiles."
	Another voice said, "He's pretty much a fixture here at Babon's. In fact, we often have a little fun with strangers. We'll give you 80 sovereigns if you can get Grimm here to laugh. Care to give it a try?"�
entries.translation:
那男人看起來不太高興。
	「他話不多，」酒館另一頭傳來一個聲音。「他這人挺陰沉的。大夥都叫他葛林姆，因為他從來不笑也不露笑臉。」
	另一個聲音說道：「他差不多算是巴本這裡的活招牌了。其實我們常拿陌生人來找點樂子。要是你能讓葛林姆笑出來，我們就給你八十枚索夫林。要不要試試看？」�

entries.source:
@4 nodded.
	"Indeed we ñwould like to give it a try," he said, then turning whispered, "Let's see...how are we going to get this fellow to laugh?"�
entries.translation:
@4點了點頭。
	「我們ñ當然願意試試，」他說道，接著轉過身低聲說：「讓我想想……我們要怎麼樣才能逗這傢伙笑呢？」�

entries.source:
@4 nodded.
	"Indeed we ñwould like to give it a try," he said, then turning whispered, "Let's see...how are we going to get this fellow to laugh?"�
entries.translation:
@4點了點頭。
	「我們ñ當然願意試試，」他說道，接著轉過身低聲說：「讓我想想……我們要怎麼樣才能逗這傢伙笑呢？」�

entries.source:
"I've got it," said @3. "This is a little trick I used to amuse my father with."
	He squatted down in front of Grimm, tipped back his head and began to sing. As the words to the silly song tumbled from his mouth he carefully balanced a spoon across the bridge of his nose.
	Grimm frowned.�
entries.translation:
「我有辦法了，」@3說道。「這是我以前用來逗我爸爸開心的小把戲。」
	他在葛林姆面前蹲下身，仰起頭，開始唱了起來。隨著這首蠢歌的歌詞從他嘴裡蹦出來，他小心翼翼地把一把湯匙平衡在鼻樑上。
	葛林姆皺起了眉頭。�

entries.source:
"ñI'll try," said @5. He turned to Grimm and with a sly smile began a bawdy tale detailing a romantic tryst between a dwarf and an elf maiden.
	Glancing around the room with a mischievous smile @5 reached the punch line, "'It just in'a gonna work,' said the dwarf, 'What with me down here and you up there.'"The end of the story brought stifled snorts and snickers from around the room, but Grimm simply nodded.�
entries.translation:
「ñ我來試試，」@5說道。他轉向葛林姆，帶著一絲狡黠的笑容，講起了一個葷段子，內容是一個矮人跟一個精靈少女的風流韻事。
	@5帶著促狹的笑容環視全場，講到了笑點：「『這根本行不通嘛，』矮人說，『畢竟我在下面，妳在上面。』」故事講完，室內傳出一片憋著的哼笑與竊笑，但葛林姆只是點了點頭。�

entries.source:
@4 stepped forward.
	"This little tale should knock him out of his chair. It was related to me by a Tsurani soldier. Seems one of their sailing ships was caught in a fierce storm that damaged the vessel so badly it began to take on water. There were rafts on board and most of the men got off safely, but it quickly became apparent to the captain that there were only three spots left and four of them still on the ship.
	'I'm going to ask each of you a question,' he said. 'Answer correctly and you can join your mates on the raft.' Turning to the first man he asked, 'ñThe ñFire ñStorm sunk off what peninsula?'
	'The Honshoni peninsula, sir.' The captain nodded and pushed the sailor toward the raft. Then he turned to the second man.
	'How many were aboard that night?' Deep in thought the second sailor finally blurted, '154!' Again, the captain nodded, pushing the sailor toward the raft. Finally, with one eye on the rising water, he turned to third man.
	'What were their names?'"
	The joke over, @4 looked at Grimm expectantly as loud guffaws filled the room and men doubled over and slapped their knees and lost ale through their noses.
	Grimm yawned.�
entries.translation:
@4站了出來。
	「這個小故事肯定能把他笑到從椅子上摔下來。這是一個圖蘭尼士兵告訴我的。說是他們有艘帆船遭遇了一場猛烈的風暴，船身受損嚴重，開始進水。船上是有救生筏的，大部分人都安全脫身了，但船長很快發現，救生筏只剩三個位置，船上卻還有四個人。
	『我要問你們每個人一個問題，』他說。『答對了，就能跟你的同伴一起上救生筏。』他轉向第一個人問道：『ñ烈焰ñ風暴ñ號是在哪個半島外海沉沒的？』
	『洪修尼半島，長官。』船長點了點頭，把那水手推向救生筏。接著他轉向第二個人。
	『那天晚上船上一共有多少人？』第二名水手苦思了半天，終於脫口而出：『一百五十四個！』船長再次點頭，把他也推向救生筏。最後，船長一邊留意著漸漸上漲的水位，一邊轉向了第三個人。
	『他們叫什麼名字？』」
	笑話講完，@4滿懷期待地看著葛林姆，室內爆出一陣哄堂大笑，眾人笑得前仰後合，拍著大腿，麥酒都從鼻子裡噴了出來。
	葛林姆打了個呵欠。�

entries.source:
@4 looked thoughtful.
	"Sumani told us a joke, does anyone remember it?" His question received nothing but blank stares.
	"Let's see if I can remember this story," he said to Grimm. "During the reign of the Hidjacumo --"
	"Hidjucama," corrected Grimm.
	"Yes... Well, the lords of the minor houses of the Omal... Omah... THREE MINOR LORDS, were summoned to the Holy City for an audience...
	...be praised! The Emperor shall love his new shoes!" finished @4, pleased he had remembered ñmost of the tale. He turned to Grimm expectantly, but found not a hint of expression on the man's face. @4 sighed in disgust, and was about to reach for his money pouch when he heard a snort, like a mad bull. He looked at Grimm. Then he looked around the room. Nothing.
	"Well, I guess we--" @4 began.
	"SNORT!" The corners of Grimm's mouth began to quiver. Then his face turned red and his body began to shake uncontrollably. It was like watching a volcano about to explode.
	"HA HA!" screamed Grimm. "Tha-- tha-- HA HA!" Tears began to clean crooked paths down the sides of his dirt streaked face, as he rolled forward and fell on the floor in spasms of uncontrollable laughter.
	There was a moment of stunned silence, then one of the men spoke, "I don't believe it! Old Grimm's actually laughing!"
	The man behind the bar produced 80 gold sovereigns. They took the money and left.�
entries.translation:
@4露出沉思的神情。
	「蘇馬尼跟我們講過一個笑話，有誰還記得嗎？」他這麼一問，換來的只有一片茫然的目光。
	「讓我看看能不能想起這個故事，」他對葛林姆說道。「在希迦庫莫在位的時候——」
	「是希杜卡瑪，」葛林姆糾正道。
	「對……總之，歐瑪……歐瑪爾……三位小家族的領主，被召去聖城覲見……
	……讚頌吧！皇帝陛下一定會喜歡他的新鞋子！」@4講完了，很滿意自己竟然記得ñ大部分的故事。他滿懷期待地轉向葛林姆，卻發現這男人臉上沒有一絲表情。@4厭惡地嘆了口氣，正打算伸手去拿錢袋時，忽然聽見一聲哼響，像頭發狂的公牛。他看向葛林姆。又環顧了一圈房間。什麼都沒有。
	「好吧，我看我們——」@4開口道。
	「哼！」葛林姆的嘴角開始顫動。接著他的臉漲得通紅，全身不受控制地抖動起來。簡直像在看一座即將噴發的火山。
	「哈哈！」葛林姆放聲大笑。「那——那——哈哈！」淚水沿著他滿是塵土的臉頰沖出一道道歪歪扭扭的痕跡，他向前一倒，跌坐在地上，笑得渾身抽搐，止不住地大笑。
	眾人一時目瞪口呆，隨後有個男人開口說道：「真不敢相信！老葛林姆居然真的笑了！」
	吧台後的男人掏出了八十枚金索夫林。他們收下錢，離開了。�

entries.source: "The man's a rock," complained @4. "I'm afraid we just can't do it."�
entries.translation: 「這傢伙簡直是塊石頭，」@4抱怨道。「恐怕我們是辦不到了。」�

entries.source:
@4 disappeared up the stairs.
	He returned a minute later shaking his head...�
entries.translation:
@4消失在樓梯上。
	一分鐘後他回來了，搖著頭……�

entries.source: "This leads off to a series of complicated mine tunnels. There may be a passage to the library vaults through there, but without a map or some directions we would ñnever find our way through."�
entries.translation: 「這裡通往一連串錯綜複雜的礦坑通道。裡頭或許有條通往藏書室地下庫的路，但沒有地圖或指引，我們ñ絕對找不到路的。」�

entries.source:
@4 disappeared up the stairs.
	He returned a minute later, a look of grim determination evident on his face...�
entries.translation:
@4消失在樓梯上。
	一分鐘後他回來了，臉上帶著一副堅毅的神情……�

entries.source: "These stairs must lead to the Mac Bourgalan Dok emerald mine. The tunnels are very complicated, but with the instructions we found in Stellan's house we should be able to make it through. Shall we try to find the library vaults?"�
entries.translation: 「這道樓梯一定通往麥克布爾加蘭多克翡翠礦坑。這些坑道非常複雜，但憑著我們在史特倫家找到的說明，應該能順利通過。要不要試著找找看藏書室地下庫？」�

entries.source:
They had been heard.
	Assembled in the book lined passage were six priests, all keenly interested in the arrival of the two strangers. From amidst them, a broad shouldered priest stepped forward.
	"óYour presence may explain a great deal," the priest said, stabbing a finger in their direction. "We have been unable to leave the vaults since this morning and we found the door is bolted from the other side. And since I find it unlikely that our brother priests of Ishap have chosen to starve us to death..."
	"It's not like that at all," @4 replied, waving his hands. "We ran into your Brother Marc when we coming up the road. He said that one of your brethren has fallen ill with the Quegian Fever and somehow his condition is linked to the passages being blocked..."
	"The mystic defenses?" one of the other priests offered. "It is possible his delusions may have triggered them."
	Quickly a debate ensued between the robed priests, finishing at last with several brethren scurrying off to shelves assigned for their examination. With a stern look, the angered priest also pointed to a shelf and directed that Owyn and Gorath look for anything that mentioned the mystic defenses of Sarth or outbreaks of Quegian Fever...�
entries.translation:
他們被人發現了。
	六名祭司聚集在這條藏書通道裡，全都對兩位陌生人的到來十分關切。一名寬肩的祭司從人群中走了出來。
	「ó你們的出現或許能解釋不少事，」那祭司說道，一根手指朝他們指去。「我們從今天早上開始就出不去，才發現門從另一頭被閂上了。既然我不太相信我們伊夏神殿的祭司兄弟們會選擇把我們活活餓死……」
	「完全不是那樣，」@4揮著手回答道。「我們上山路時碰到了你們的馬克修士。他說你們有位兄弟染上了奎格熱病，而他的病情不知為何跟這通道被封鎖的事有所關聯……」
	「是那道神祕防禦嗎？」另一名祭司提議道。「有可能是他的譫語觸發了它。」
	身穿長袍的祭司們很快展開了一場爭論，最後幾位教友匆匆散開，去查看各自被指派的書架。那名發怒的祭司神情嚴厲地也指了一個書架，指示歐文和戈拉斯去找任何提到薩斯神祕防禦或奎格熱病爆發的記載……�

entries.source:
Hours passed.
	His eyes aching from reading the nearly illegible handwriting of ancient scribes, @4 leaned his head back against the ancient shelving. "I have no idea what we're looking for, Gorath. I've run across a half dozen references to this Abbey, but then I discover it has something to do with experiments with peas or an account of a new system of organizing these books..."
	A sound drew their attention. At the end of the book strewn passageway in which they sat, a priest eyed the disorganization with distress. "Why are you still down here?"
	"Still looking for the answer," @4 said. Vaguely he gestured at the half dozen opened books around him. "Haven't found it."
	"Oh." Biting his lip, the priest seemed pensive about continuing. "Well, I am afraid we solved that problem about an hour ago. Brother Dominic is doing a bit better now. We were wondering where you two had gotten to."
	Angered, @4 slammed shut the cover of the book which he held in his lap, a translation of ãDãoãrãcãaãsã'ã ãTãrãeãaãtãiãsãeã ãOãnã ãTãhãeã ãAãnãiãmãaãtãiãoãnã ãoãfã ãOãbãjãeãcãtãs. Likewise, next to him, Gorath stuffed away a wormy looking book on history.
	"Keep it," the priest insisted before Owyn could put away the magical treatise. "Dorcas' is popular here. We have other copies cross indexed in the library. I was also instructed that once I found you, I was to reward you with these..."
	Opening a pouch, the priest handed them three nearly perfect emeralds. "They are yours, in appreciation for all you have done here. It is a small gesture, but I hope a useful one. Please feel free to continue to scan our library if it please you..."�
entries.translation:
幾個鐘頭過去了。
	看著古代抄寫員那幾乎難以辨認的字跡，@4看得雙眼發痠，把頭靠回了那座古老的書架上。「我完全不知道我們在找什麼，戈拉斯。我已經翻到六七處提到這座修道院的記載了，但不是發現跟豌豆實驗有關，就是跟一套新的圖書分類系統有關……」
	一陣聲響引起了他們的注意。在他們所坐的書堆通道盡頭，一名祭司神情不悅地打量著這片凌亂。「你們怎麼還在這下面？」
	「還在找答案呢，」@4說道。他含糊地朝身邊那半打攤開的書比了比。「還沒找到。」
	「哦。」那祭司咬著嘴唇，似乎猶豫著要不要繼續說下去。「呃，恐怕我們大概一個鐘頭前就解決那個問題了。多明尼克修士現在好多了。我們正在想你們兩位到底跑哪去了。」
	@4又氣又惱，把手中那本書「啪」地一聲闔上——那是一本ã多ã卡ã斯ã所ã著ã《ã論ã以ã秘ã法ã賦ã予ã尋ã常ã器ã物ã以ã生ã命ã與ã意ã志ã動ã作ã之ã奧ã祕ã要ã義ã完ã整ã精ã校ã考ã訂ã全ã新ã譯ã本ã附ã錄ã詳ã注ã》的譯本。與此同時，坐在一旁的戈拉斯也把一本看起來蟲蛀嚴重的史書收了起來。
	「留著吧，」還沒等歐文把那本魔法論著收起來，祭司便堅持道。「多卡斯的書在這裡很受歡迎。我們圖書館裡還有其他交叉索引的抄本。我也奉命，等找到你們之後，要拿這些東西酬謝你們……」
	祭司打開一個小袋子，遞給他們三顆近乎完美的翡翠。「這些是給你們的，感謝你們在這裡所做的一切。這只是個小小心意，但我希望能派上用場。要是你們願意，也歡迎繼續瀏覽我們的圖書館……」�

entries.source:
The door swung open.
	"Good day to you fine sirs," said the man at the door. "My name is Franklin Hurley, how can I be of service to you?"
	@4 cleared his throat. "We were told at the Temple of Silban that you might want to see us."

	Franklin excitedly retreated into his house and returned a moment later with a pouch of coins that he demanded they take as a reward. @4 tried to turn the money down, but the man insisted.
	They thanked him for his kindness and generosity, then they left.�
entries.translation:

	@4清了清嗓子。「我們在席爾班神殿聽說，你可能想找我們談談。」
	「你們跟女祭司們談過了？」他難以置信地問道。「我本想找她們談談明年收成的事，卻有三個大呼小叫的蠢貨不讓我過去。」
	「你不會再被那三個人找麻煩了，」@5說。
	富蘭克林興奮地退回屋裡，片刻後拿著一袋錢幣出來，硬要他們收下作為酬謝。@4試著婉拒，但那男人堅持不肯。
	他們謝過他的好意與慷慨，隨後便離開了。�

entries.source:

	@4 was about to ask him another question when Chanty suddenly mumbled something angrily and slammed the door closed. No amount of coaxing could convince him to open it again.�
entries.translation:
在門口迎接他們的男人身上有股魚腥味。
	「大夥都叫我強提，」@4自我介紹後，他這麼回應道。
	又閒聊了幾分鐘，他才透露自己是個漁夫，但由於身體不適，已經好幾天沒出海了。他說話時，還不時朝@0肩後某個看不見的東西投去陰沉的眼神。
	@4正要再問他一個問題，強提卻突然氣呼呼地嘟噥了一句，砰地一聲把門關上了。任憑怎麼勸說，都沒法讓他再把門打開。�

entries.source:
"Have you seen my gold?" asked the man at the door.
	"I'm afraid we haven't," said @4. "Aren't you Chanty the fisherman?" he questioned.
	"Yes, but I didn't mean to do it," he replied wildly. "I was looking for my gold, I didn't know it was still...alive." He shivered involuntarily.
	@4 looked at @0, then continued, playing along though he wasn't sure what the man was talking about. "But you ñdid do it. Why don't you tell us about it?"
	Shaking harder, Chanty said, "It was a black thing...I dug and dug... then it grabbed my arm and I pulled away but it wouldn't let go and then it clawed its way out... and it ñtalked to me. The demon thing spoke to me and... and... ñthanked me for letting it go." He stopped, nearly in tears. "It even gave me a reward. It gave me passwords for a couple of the local fairy chests. Said they were: ñeyes and ñringð."
	Unable to control his fear any longer, he retreated into his house, slamming the door.�
entries.translation:
「你們看到我的金子了嗎？」門口那男人問道。
	「恐怕沒有，」@4說。「你不是漁夫強提嗎？」他問道。
	「是啊，可我不是故意的，」他語無倫次地回答。「我只是在找我的金子，我不知道它還……活著。」他不由自主地打了個寒顫。
	@4看了看@0，接著繼續順著他的話說下去，儘管他不太明白這男人在說什麼。「但你ñ確實這麼做了。何不跟我們說說詳情？」
	強提抖得更厲害了，說道：「那是個黑色的東西……我挖啊挖……然後它抓住了我的手臂，我想抽開，它卻不肯放，接著它就自己爬了出來……而且它ñ跟我說話了。那個惡魔般的東西跟我說話，還……還……ñ謝謝我放它走。」他停了下來，幾乎要落淚。「它甚至還給了我獎賞。它給了我幾個附近精靈寶箱的密語。說是：ñ眼睛和ñ戒指ð。」
	再也無法控制心中的恐懼，他退回屋裡，砰地一聲關上了門。�

entries.source:
A man answered @4's knock.
	His face was flushed and there were beads of sweat on his brow that threatened to race each other down his face at any moment. He was breathing heavily.
	"You've come about ñthem haven't you?" he asked, wide eyed. "Well?"
	After several long minutes of careful probing, @4 was able to ascertain that the man believed he had released some evil spirits from a couple of the local graveyards. The more he spoke of his dealings with the undead the more frightened he became, until at last, shivering violently, he closed the door and retreated back into the relative safety of his house.�

entries.translation:

entries.source:
The man joined them.
	"What can I do for you?" he asked.
	@4 offered the man a seat. "What can you tell us of the area?" he asked.
	"You won't be wanting to travel by night, sirs. Rusalki roam the hills lookin' for weary travelers to prey upon. And truth be known?" he lowered his voice to a whisper. "ñI think the innkeeper has somethin' to do with it."
	"What makes you think that?" @4 said with a tilt of his head.
	The man looked around, "People say he knew where the Rusalki were hemmed in during the day, and that he hired a fella named Crenard and a few of his companions to ñprotect it!"
	Head still atilt, @4 asked, "Why would he want to do that?"
	"To protect his livelihood, o' course! Folks was scared to sleep outdoors, so they would stay at his inn -- he was makin' a pile of the shiny stuff, he was."�
entries.translation:
那男人加入了他們。
	「有什麼能為你們效勞的？」他問道。
	@4請那男人坐下。「你能跟我們說說這一帶的情況嗎？」他問道。
	「兩位先生，你們可不會想夜裡趕路的。露莎卡在這些山丘間遊蕩，尋找疲憊的旅人下手。而說實話呢？」他把聲音壓低成耳語。「ñ我覺得客棧老闆跟這事脫不了干係。」
	「你為什麼這麼想？」@4歪著頭問道。
	那男人四下張望，說：「有人說他白天就知道露莎卡藏在哪裡，還雇了個叫克雷納德的傢伙，帶著他的幾個同伴去ñ保護那個地方！」
	@4依然歪著頭，問道：「他為什麼要那麼做？」
	「當然是為了保住自己的生意啊！大家都怕在外頭露宿，於是就跑來投宿他的旅店——他可是狠狠賺了一筆呢。」�

entries.source:
Bella said nothing as he let them inside.
	Next to the door, Haphra was sitting up, her frail fingers clutched in her hair and a distant look on her face. As she regarded them, she looked more relieved than pained for her injury. "She is dead?"
	"Yes," @4 replied. "Dead. Or at least we may assume so. What exactly did we witness here?"
	"A foolish old woman who didn't wish to let her daughter go," she said, her voice trembling. Grabbing hold of Bella's hand for support, she continued on bravely. "After our daughter died, I sought to find her with my talents. I thought if I could seize on to her, we could keep her with us."
	"But that's not what you found," @4 replied.
	Haphra shook her head. "No it wasn't. Instead, I found the spirit of the rusalki who promised that she would bring our daughter to us, if we would allow her to live through me, to inhabit this body. For a while we believed her, but after several weeks...we knew we had been trapped by the creature."
	Feeling awkward in the woman's presence, @4 touched the woman's shoulder lightly. "I am very sorry."
	"Don't be," she said. "You have freed us of a curse and now we can begin to rebuild our lives without my daughter. For this, I shall grant you a ñtrue prophecy, or at least one as true as I am capable."�
entries.translation:
貝拉一言不發地讓他們進了門。
	門邊，哈芙拉正坐著，一雙纖細的手指緊揪著自己的頭髮，眼神望向遠方。她看著他們，臉上與其說是痛苦，不如說是如釋重負。「她死了？」
	「是的，」@4回答道。「死了。至少我們可以這麼推斷。我們到底目睹了什麼？」
	「一個不肯放手讓女兒離開的傻老太婆，」她說道，聲音顫抖著。她抓住貝拉的手尋求支撐，鼓起勇氣繼續說了下去。「我們女兒死後，我試著用我的能力找到她。我想，要是我能抓住她，我們就能把她留在身邊。」
	「但你找到的不是她，」@4接話道。
	哈芙拉搖了搖頭。「沒錯，不是。相反地，我找到的是露莎卡的靈魂，她答應會把我們女兒帶回來，只要我們讓她透過我活下去，寄居在這具身體裡。有一陣子，我們相信了她，但過了幾個星期……我們才明白，我們已經被這個怪物困住了。」
	在這位婦人面前感到有些不自在，@4輕輕碰了碰她的肩膀。「我很遺憾。」
	「不必遺憾，」她說。「你們解除了我們身上的詛咒，如今我們終於能不帶著女兒的陰影，重新開始生活了。為此，我要給你們一個ñ真正的預言，至少，是我能力所及最真實的一個。」�

entries.source:
Looking deep into @4's eyes, Haphra spoke slowly. "You will face an adversary who's life force is not as your own," she said. "It will be in a far away place and you will have to draw on their strength rather than their life to defeat them. And I sense that you alone will not be capable, for there will be another who is like yourself, another magician."
	"What is his name?" @4 asked, intrigued by the answer.
	"I do not know," the woman replied in shame, looking to the floor. "In truth, my powers are quite limited. I have told you all that I can truly see."
	"Enough," Bella said. "It is time you had some rest, Haphra."
	Understanding that the man wished for them to leave, @4 nodded thankfully to the fortune teller and her husband. "Good luck on your new life together," he said, closing the door behind them. "I think you deserve it."�
entries.translation:

	「他叫什麼名字？」@4問道，對這個答案很感興趣。
	「我不知道，」那婦人羞愧地回答，垂眼望向地面。「說實話，我的能力相當有限。我能真正看見的，都已經告訴你們了。」
	「夠了，」貝拉說道。「哈芙拉，你該休息了。」

"Futures, speaking with the dead, rumors. We will require a payment of fifty gold. Do you wish a session with Madame?"�

一個男人出現在門口。

entries.source:
@4 produced the requested amount and handed it over, following the tall man. Just before pushing aside a curtain, he halted and whispered to them.
	"Do not question some of the things my wife may say or do," he said. "We have recently lost a daughter and it has shaken Haphra's belief in some of her...óabilities. Please, if she asks for acceptance, no matter what she may have said, please treat her kindly."
	Without another word, he shoved aside the curtain and allowed them into a rear room where Madame Haphra waited. Seated at a table, she wore a woven brocade vest over a lightly dyed peasant's blouse, and her hands and neck were ornamented with bright wooden beads.
	"Please have a seat," she muttered, waving a brightly nailed hand at the rude chairs set across from her. As she spoke, her eyelids fluttered, as if she were speaking through an alcoholic haze. "I may provide three services for you. We may speak of local rumors, I may tell thee the future, or I may speak to the dead. Which would you have of me?"�
entries.translation:

	「請坐，」她低聲說道，朝對面那幾張簡陋的椅子揮了揮塗著鮮豔指甲油的手。她說話時，眼皮半闔半開地顫動著，彷彿是透過一層酒醉的迷霧在說話。「我能為你們提供三種服務。我們可以聊聊當地的傳聞，我可以告訴你們未來，或是我可以與死者對話。你們想要哪一種？」�

"I do not believe they were finished," she said, treating them with a faint smile. "For the price you they have paid, they may continue to ask questions. So, strangers. As I have told you before, we may speak of local rumors, I may tell thee the future, or I may speak to the dead. Which would you have of me?"�
entries.translation: 貝拉以為這場問卜已經結束，正要上前送客，哈芙拉卻示意他留在原地。「我看他們還沒問完，」她說道，帶著一抹淡淡的微笑望著他們。「憑你們付的這個價錢，還可以繼續發問。所以，陌生人們。就像我先前說的，我們可以聊聊當地的傳聞，我可以告訴你們未來，或是我可以與死者對話。你們想要哪一種？」�

entries.source:
"Rumors," she repeated, quietly. Leaning forward in her seat, she met @4's gaze and held it, allowing her voice to harden. "Rumors? I will tell thee of the only rumor about which I know. Many have come and spoken to me of Rusalki that roam the lands near the River Pilot's Folly at night, but these are ólies..."
	Startled with the ferocity with which the woman had bitten off the last word, @4 shrugged his shoulders. "I had not heard anything of them..."
	"Do not seek the Rusalki!" she continued, her voice still frantic. "They are of no harm to anyone!"
	Although he had remained quiet as Haphra had begun to rant, Bella moved forward and touched her on the shoulder, seemingly relieving the wildness that was overcoming her. "These gentlemen are friends," he said quietly. "You will not be injured."
	Taking his hand, she nodded once, then looked back at @4. "You will forgive me. This has...ótouched our lives, but I can explain no further."�
entries.translation:
「傳聞，」她輕聲重複道。她在座位上向前傾身，迎上@4的目光，直視不移，聲音也隨之變得冷硬。「傳聞？我就告訴你們我唯一知道的傳聞吧。不少人來跟我提過，說夜裡有露莎卡在領航員之愚河附近的土地上遊蕩，但這些都是ó謊言……」
	被這婦人咬字時透出的凶狠嚇了一跳，@4聳了聳肩。「我倒沒聽說過這事……」
	「別去找那些露莎卡！」她的聲音依然帶著幾分狂亂，繼續說道。「她們對誰都沒有傷害！」
	哈芙拉開始語無倫次時，貝拉一直靜靜待在一旁，這時他上前輕輕碰了碰她的肩膀，似乎緩解了她心頭湧起的那股狂躁。「這幾位先生是朋友，」他輕聲說道。「你不會受到傷害的。」
	她握住他的手，點了點頭，隨後回頭望向@4。「請你們原諒我。這件事……ó牽動了我們的人生，但我沒法再多說什麼了。」�

entries.source: "Very well," Haphra said with a weak smile, her posture relaxing visibly as she leaned back into the overstuffed cushions of her sitting chair. "We shall tell your future..."�
entries.translation: 「好吧，」哈芙拉露出一絲虛弱的微笑說道，靠回她座椅上鬆軟的靠墊，姿態明顯放鬆了下來。「我們來看看你們的未來……」�

entries.source: @4 cringed as he found that the mystic was regarding him intensely, fixing him with a gaze that looked frankly more familiar than he liked. "You shall discover wealth in a hidden place, but shall lose something dearly won so that you may obtain it. In gaining it, you shall have great joy, but later will find that it holds great misery for the time ahead."�
entries.translation: @4不禁畏縮了一下，發現這位靈媒正緊盯著他，那目光坦白說比他所希望的還要熟悉幾分。「你將在一處隱密之地發現財富，但為了得到它，你將失去某樣得來不易的東西。得到它時，你會感到莫大的喜悅，但日後你會發現，未來的日子裡它其實藏著莫大的痛苦。」�

entries.source: Staring deep into @4's eyes, she hesitated a moment, then shook her head. "I can tell you nothing you do not already know," she said, then locked gazes with @5. "But you, however, I see betrayal in your future. You will turn on all that you have sworn oath to and will become something you once hated. You will face your enemy most hated and he will change you."�
entries.translation: 深深望進@4的雙眼，她遲疑了片刻，隨後搖了搖頭。「我沒什麼能告訴你的，你早已心知肚明，」她說道，接著把目光鎖定在@5身上。「但你，我卻在你的未來裡看見了背叛。你會背棄自己曾發誓效忠的一切，變成自己曾經憎惡的模樣。你將面對自己最痛恨的敵人，而他會改變你。」�

entries.source: For a long moment she sat silently, her gaze turned as much inwards as outwards, but at last she spoke in a startlingly youthful voice. "A long shadow and a star stand over your house," she said, addressing @4. "Even as you find the soul that is kin to your own and achieve all that you had hoped, you will lose your closest friend to passion in a foreign land."�
entries.translation: 有好長一段時間，她靜靜坐著，目光既望向內心，也望向外界，最後她終於開口，聲音出奇地年輕。「一道長長的陰影與一顆星辰籠罩著你的家門，」她對@4說道。「即便你找到了與自己心靈相通的另一半，實現了你所盼望的一切，你也將在異鄉，因一段激情而失去你最親近的朋友。」�

entries.source: Regarding @3, the look on her face slowly changed, turning into a mask of pain and regret. "You will die a slow and painful death, alone and in starvation," she said somberly. "Those upon whom you thought you could count will abandon you in your hour of need and in death they will believe you a disgrace to your station."�
entries.translation: 望著@3，她臉上的神情漸漸變了，化作一副痛苦與悔恨交織的面容。「你將孤獨一人，在飢餓中緩慢而痛苦地死去，」她語氣沉重地說道。「你曾以為能夠依靠的人，將在你最需要的時刻棄你而去，而在你死後，他們也會認為你玷污了自己的身分。」�

entries.source:
A puzzled look crossed Haphra's face as she attempted to concentrate.
	"Yours is a fortune I have not seen the like of for some time. A dead man's key will open the doors which cannot be seen and are hidden beneath those who bow below the seven rayed star."�
entries.translation:
哈芙拉臉上閃過一絲困惑，努力集中著精神。
	「你的命運，我已經很久沒見過這樣的了。一把死人的鑰匙，將開啟那些看不見的門，它們藏在向七芒星俯首的人之下。」�

entries.source: Her eyes half-closed, she looked dreamily at @4, licking her lips as she spoke. "When you are driven on the longest road, you will seek to destroy the instrument of deception, but will find need to deceive those who guard the way. In the very last place you will find that salvation is with the man who seems a boy."�
entries.translation: 她半闔著雙眼，恍惚地望著@4，說話時舔了舔嘴唇。「當你被逼上那條最漫長的道路時，你會想摧毀那件矇騙人心的器物，卻發現自己必須欺瞞守路之人。而在最後一刻，你將發現，救贖竟在一個看似孩子的男人身上。」�

entries.source: Shivering, as if seized with a sudden chill, she flicked a bony finger out at @3. "You shall save one whom you admire from a dire fate, but shall awaken the attention of those whom most wish for your destruction. Forever after, you shall find that you walk the paths of the world nameless and alone."�
entries.translation: 彷彿突然被一陣寒意攫住，她顫抖著，伸出一根瘦骨嶙峋的手指指向@3。「你將從一場致命的厄運中拯救你所敬重的人，卻也因此喚起了那些最盼望你毀滅之人的注意。從此以後，你將發現自己在世間漂泊，無名亦無伴。」�

entries.source: Folding her hands in her lap, she looked on them serenely, her face beginning to resume the look of her age. "This is the fate I see for you," she said, the slight tremolo in her voice betraying a hint of nervousness. "The fates have spoken through me..."�
entries.translation: 她把手交疊在膝上，平靜地望著他們，臉上漸漸恢復了她這個年紀該有的神情。「這就是我為你們看見的命運，」她說道，聲音裡帶著一絲微微的顫抖，透露出些許緊張。「命運已經藉由我開口了……」�

entries.source: Detecting how important it was to the fortune teller that they believed what she had told them, @4 leaned forward and patted the old woman's hands. "We believe you Haphra," he said, reinforcing his words with a flashed smile.�
entries.translation: 察覺到讓他們相信自己所說的話對這位算命師有多重要，@4傾身向前，輕拍了拍老婦人的手。「我們相信你，哈芙拉，」他說道，臉上還閃過一抹笑容，加強了語氣。�

entries.source:
@4 snorted his contempt for the old woman's prediction. "I could have said any of the same things. I've heard virtually all those things from street lunatics..."
	"Haphra!" Bella shouted, but was shoved aside like a mere twig as the old woman lunged to her feet, her eyes blazing fury. Raking @4's face with her sharpened nails, she howled in a voice that no longer sounded human. "ãIã ãaãmã ãHãaãpãhãrãaã!ã ãYãoãuã ãwãiãlãlã ãbãeãlãiãeãvãeã!ã ãYãoãuã ãwãiãlãlã ãbãeãlãiãeãvãeã.ã.ã."
	Weeping openly, Bella moved behind his distraught wife, but rather than trying to console her, he lifted a stick of firewood and struck her to the floor. Standing over her unconscious form, he seemed poised to strike again.
	"Wha...," Confused, @4 flashed a horrified stare at Bella, but suddenly drew back in shock as another form began to materialize around Haphra's crumpled body, taking on the shape of a young girl. For a moment it hovered, its expression glowering as it stared at Bella. Then, with a hateful screech, it flashed through the air to pass through the walls of the house.
	"Go after it," Bella sobbed, dropping to the ground to cradle his wife. "Go and kill it. We are finished with the rusalki now. Go!"
	Nearly tripping over the clutter of the small house, they rushed outside and prepared their weapons for the rusalki who now awaited to kill them all...�
entries.translation:
@4對這老婦人的預言嗤之以鼻。「這些話我隨便也能說出來。街上那些瘋子講的話我大概都聽過了……」
	「哈芙拉！」貝拉喊道，卻像根細枝般被一把推開，那老婦人猛地站起身，雙眼燃著怒火。她用磨尖的指甲抓向@4的臉，發出一聲已不再像人類的咆哮：「ã我ã是ã哈ã芙ã拉ã！ã你ã會ã相ã信ã的ã！ã你ã會ã相ã信ã的ã！ã你ã會ã相ã信ã的ã！ã你ã會ã相ã信ã的ã！ã你ã會ã相ã信ã的ã！ã你ã會ã相ã信ã的ã！ã你ã會ã相ã信ã的ã！ã…ã…」
	貝拉公然哭了出來，繞到他那失魂落魄的妻子身後，但他沒有試著安撫她，反而舉起一根木柴，把她打倒在地。他站在她昏迷不醒的身軀上方，彷彿隨時準備再次揮下。
	「什……」@4困惑地朝貝拉投去一個驚駭的眼神，卻突然驚恐地後退，只見另一個身形開始在哈芙拉癱倒的身軀周圍浮現，逐漸化作一個少女的模樣。它懸浮了片刻，神情陰沉地瞪著貝拉，接著發出一聲充滿恨意的尖嘯，颯地穿牆而去。
	「追上去，」貝拉啜泣著說道，跪倒在地，摟住了他的妻子。「去把它殺了。我們跟露莎卡之間的事，就此了結了。快去！」
	他們幾乎被小屋裡的雜物絆倒，衝出屋外，握緊武器，準備迎戰那頭如今正等著要取他們性命的露莎卡……�

entries.source: Closing her eyes, the old woman shook as if a tree bowing beneath the winds of a howling gale, her lips drawn taut and her face drained of color. After several moments of effort, she shook her head. "I cannot...help you. Lims-Kragma holds those you wish too tightly."�
entries.translation: 老婦人閉上雙眼，渾身顫抖，彷彿一棵在狂風中彎腰的樹，嘴唇緊繃，臉上血色盡失。過了好一會兒，她搖了搖頭。「我沒辦法……幫你們。林絲克拉格瑪把你們想找的人抓得太緊了。」�

entries.source: Placing a hand to her temples, Haphra motioned for Bella to come forward. "I have grown ñweary from this," she said. "Bella will show you to the door. You may come back another time if you wish to know more."�
entries.translation: 哈芙拉把手按上太陽穴，示意貝拉上前。「這事讓我感到ñ疲憊不堪，」她說道。「貝拉會送你們出去。要是你們想知道更多，改天再回來吧。」�

Noticing that @5 appeared to be drifting off, @4 threw him a sympathetic smile. "I think we've heard enough for now, Madame Haphra. Perhaps we will come and see you again."
	"Very well," she replied. "Bella shall show you out."�

注意到@5似乎快要打起瞌睡，@4朝他投去一個體諒的微笑。「我想我們現在聽得也夠多了，哈芙拉夫人。或許改天我們會再來拜訪你。」

A voice inside the house called out to them.
	"Go away! Lord Lyton is very busy meeting with a reeve sent from Earl Presser, and he doesn't wish to be disturbed at the moment."
	They argued with the voice behind the door for several minutes, then, recognizing the futility of further discussion, left.�
entries.translation:
屋裡傳出一個聲音，朝他們喊道。
	「走開！萊頓爵爺正忙著跟普雷瑟伯爵派來的一名執行官會面，此刻不希望被打擾。」
	他們跟門後那個聲音爭論了好幾分鐘，最後意識到再爭下去也是徒勞，便離開了。�

entries.source:
A servant met them at the door.
	She ushered them inside and led them to a partitioned corner of the room. Pulling back the curtain, she revealed a gangly man with a white beard and snow grey hair who introduced himself as Lord Lyton.
	"Please forgive my humble accommodations," he sighed. "My financial situation has been compromised by the death of my lord, Earl Presser of Romney." Suddenly, he brightened, "Perhaps you fine gentlemen would be willing to assist me in a small matter..."
	"What could we do to help you?" asked @4.
	The lord sighed again, "I was to equip six knights and send them to Romney for my former lord, but his holdings were bestowed on his half-brother following his death, and ñhe wishes me to deliver ñ12 fully equipped knights to ñMalac's Cross."
	"If you could bring me 6 suits of kingdom armor, in good condition, I would be able to get rid of those annoying tax collectors who have been travelling the roads terrorizing people and extorting money. I wouldn't actually expect that you would have that sort of a thing with you. You don't do you?"�
entries.translation:
一名僕人在門口迎接了他們。
	她領著他們進屋，帶到房間一處用簾子隔開的角落。她拉開簾子，露出一個瘦高、留著白鬍子、滿頭灰白頭髮的男人，他自我介紹說自己是萊頓爵爺。
	「請原諒我這寒酸的住處，」他嘆了口氣。「我的財務狀況因我主人——羅姆尼的普雷瑟伯爵——過世而陷入了困境。」他忽然眼睛一亮，「或許幾位好心的先生願意幫我個小忙……」
	「我們能幫上什麼忙？」@4問道。
	這位爵爺又嘆了口氣，「我原本該替我已故的主人裝備六名騎士，送去羅姆尼，但他的產業在他過世後由異母兄弟繼承了，那人ñ要我送ñ十二名全副武裝的騎士去ñ馬拉克十字鎮。
	「要是你們能給我帶來六套狀況良好的王國鎧甲，我就能擺脫那些在路上騷擾百姓、敲詐勒索的煩人稅吏了。我倒是不指望你們身上正好帶著這種東西。你們該不會有吧？」�

entries.source:
@4 made a face. "It isn't ñexactly the sort of thing we would carry about with us as a rule."
	"Of course not," Lyton replied, showing them to the door. "But please, see what you can do."�

	"Glad we could help," said @4 nobly.

entries.translation:

entries.source:
A man shouted to them.
	"Have you brought the Chief Reeve's dinner?" he asked, evidently viewing their arrival as part of a regular schedule. When @4 wasn't quick to respond, the man seemed to get a bit irritated. "Are you or aren't you the delivery men from the goods store?"
	"Yes," @4 quickly lied, seeing it as an obvious way to get past the guard. "We'll just go on in and deliver his dinner to him..."
	The man frowned. "Obviously they didn't explain to you the way things work round here. No one comes past Podrich," he said, thumping his chest. "You go over next to the field and put the goods in the box, then go about your way. Now do you or don't you have his food?"�
entries.translation:
一個男人朝他們喊話。
	「你們把首席執行官的晚餐帶來了嗎？」他問道，顯然把他們的到來當成了例行公事的一部分。@4沒能立刻回應，那男人似乎有點不耐煩了。「你們到底是不是雜貨店派來的送貨人？」
	「是，」@4立刻扯了個謊，覺得這是矇混過守衛最簡單的辦法。「我們這就進去，把晚餐送給他……」
	那男人皺起眉頭。「看來沒人跟你們解釋過這裡的規矩。沒人能繞過波德里奇，」他說著，用力拍了拍自己的胸口。「你們得繞到那片田地旁邊，把貨放進箱子裡，然後就可以走了。現在，你們到底有沒有帶他的食物？」�

entries.source:
The man grumbled.
	Not sure whether the comment was an invitation or an indication they should leave, @4 approached the man cautiously. "Good day."
	"Good day my arse. Damn madness, all this guild feuding," he spat, wiping ale from his lips with the back of his hand. "I had a regular job before all this madness began up in Romney. Now I have to do my job under the cover of night. If Arlie Steelsoul would come to the negotiations table with the rest of the Guilds, we could bring this idiocy to a halt!"
	"Has anyone talked to him?" @4 asked.
	"Who can?" the man replied. "He's got himself sealed up in his house near Sloop. None of the Duke of Romney's men have been able to get through to him. He won't even allow his supplies to be delivered to his door anymore, has them dropped off in a box. Serve him right if someone sent in a pack of rations that had been sitting in the sun a month or more, arrogant bastard. Know how much it costs me to harbor my flats now? 100 sovereigns every two weeks!"
	Despite @4 repeated attempts to steer the conversation in a more interesting direction, the man insisted in relating his docking fees at the various points along the river and the outrageous lengths to which he had to resort to deliver his goods unmolested. At last, the effect of his ale beginning to overwhelm him, he slumped against the wall and began to snore...�
entries.translation:
那男人咕噥了一句。
	不確定這句話是邀請還是要他們離開的暗示，@4小心翼翼地靠近了這男人。「日安。」
	「日安個屁。都是這場公會鬥爭鬧出的荒唐事，」他啐了一口，用手背抹去唇邊的麥酒。「在這場鬧劇開始之前，我有份正經工作。現在我得趁著夜色掩護才能幹活。要是亞利鋼魂肯跟其他公會一起坐下來談判，我們早就能了結這場愚蠢的鬧劇了！」
	「有人找他談過嗎？」@4問道。
	「誰找得到他？」那男人回答道。「他把自己關在斯魯普附近的家裡，誰都進不去。羅姆尼公爵派去的人一個都沒能見到他。他現在連補給都不讓人送到家門口了，全都得放進箱子裡才行。要是有人送一批曬了一個月太陽的口糧給他，也算他活該，那個傲慢的混蛋。你知道我現在光是停靠我那些平底船要花多少錢嗎？每兩個星期一百枚索夫林！」
	儘管@4一再試著把話題引向更有意思的方向，這男人卻堅持講起了他在河邊各個碼頭要繳的停靠費，還有他為了順利送貨不得不忍受的種種荒唐苛索。最後，麥酒的醉意終於占了上風，他癱靠在牆邊，打起了呼嚕……�

entries.source:
The Reeve met them at the door.
	Nearly bald except for a few short tufts of hair which cropped behind his ears like untended weeds, the Chief Reeve was a surprisingly small man for the position of power he held among the Guilds of the Romney. Smiling fiercely at them, he slapped @4's shoulder with a heat blistered hand.
	"Arlie Steelsoul here," he said. "If nothing else, you've got chutzpah. Lucky I didn't eat the stuff you dropped in the box without having it checked first. Learned a long time ago to be wary of trusting people on the outside."�
entries.translation:
那位執行官在門口迎接了他們。
	這人幾乎全禿，只剩耳後幾撮短短的雜毛，像疏於照料的雜草。以他在羅姆尼各公會之間掌握的權勢而言，這位首席執行官身材出奇矮小。他朝他們露出凶狠的笑容，用一隻長滿水泡的手拍了拍@4的肩膀。
	「我是亞利鋼魂，」他說。「不管怎麼說，你們膽子倒是不小。還好我沒不經檢查就把你們放進箱子裡的東西給吃了。我很早以前就學到教訓，得提防外人。」�

entries.source:
He invited them into his home, offered them some food and water and spoke of the guild war near Romney. "It started when the Riverpullers jacked their prices so high no one could afford to ship things down river," he explained. "That forced Mitchel Waylander to turn to the Guild of the Romney -- well, let me tell you, Chief Reeve of the Riverpullers didn't like ñthat at all -- felt the new guild was trying to undercut his business, but can you blame him? Mitchel, I mean."
	@4 shook his head. "The Duke of Romney doesn't seem too happy about matters either," he said. "He wants you to come to the negotiations table so they can bring a halt to the violence in Romney."
	Arlie nodded. "Bloody politics started this mess and it looks like that's what it'll take to bring it to an end. They'll take a chunk out of the Ironmonger's Guild, be sure of that. We've always lost at the negotiations table."
	"Then we can tell the Duke you ówill negotiate?" @4 asked.
	Walking to a row of shelves, he pulled down a book. "Nothing else to do that I know of." Alerting @4 first, he tossed the tome. "Thought you might like this after all your questions about the ironwork..."
	"What is it?" @4 asked, looking at the plain leather cover.
	"A beginner's text on the art of repairing arms and armor. I was going to throw it out to make room for a few new books that Podrich brought to me. You're welcome to it."
	Thanking the Reeve for his generous offer, @4 motioned to @5 it was time they were on their way once again. "We will tell the Duke," he said before closing the door. "He will be excited I think."�
entries.translation:
他邀請他們進屋，端出了些食物與水，聊起了羅姆尼附近的公會之爭。「這事的起因，是拉船工會把運價哄抬得太高，沒人負擔得起走水路運貨了，」他解釋道。「這逼得米契爾威蘭德轉而投靠羅姆尼公會——好吧，我跟你說，拉船工會的首席執行官對ñ這事可不太高興——覺得這個新公會是在搶他的生意，但你能怪他嗎？我是說米契爾。」
	@4搖了搖頭。「羅姆尼公爵對這件事似乎也不太滿意，」他說。「他希望你能坐上談判桌，好平息羅姆尼這場暴力衝突。」
	亞利點了點頭。「是骯髒的政治把這場亂子鬧出來的，看來也只能靠政治手段來收場了。他們一定會從鐵匠公會身上狠狠割一塊肉，這點你放心。我們在談判桌上向來吃虧。」
	「那我們可以告訴公爵你ó會參與談判嗎？」@4問道。
	他走到一排書架前，抽出一本書。先跟@4打了聲招呼，才把那本書扔了過去。「我不知道還有什麼別的辦法。」「想說你問了這麼多鐵器相關的問題，大概會喜歡這個……」
	「這是什麼？」@4問道，看著那樸素的皮革封面。
	「一本入門級的武器盔甲修繕手冊。我本來打算扔了，好給波德里奇送來的幾本新書騰個地方。你就拿去用吧。」
	謝過這位執行官的慷慨相贈，@4朝@5示意，是時候再度上路了。「我們會轉告公爵，」他說道，隨即關上了門。「我想他一定會很高興。」�

entries.source:
Waving them inside, he took them on a short tour of his home, displaying a number of new and interesting bits of ironwork that he had been given by friends within the Ironmonger's Guild. When at last he had run out of rooms and breath, he politely escorted them back to the door.
	"I'm glad we got this chance to talk," he said. "Been a while since I've had a chance to gab with anyone outside of Podrich."
	"Maybe you shouldn't keep yourself locked up in a cage," @4 said. "While you might be keeping out potential enemies, you're also keeping out potential allies."
	"Thought about that," he admitted. "It's just this whole mess with what's happening in Romney. I'll take it under advisement. Either way, you lot will be welcome anytime you'd like to come back and visit. Watch you don't get yourselves skinned!"�
entries.translation:
他招手示意他們進屋，帶他們簡單參觀了一下自己的住處，展示了幾件他從鐵匠公會的朋友那裡得來、既新奇又有趣的鐵器。等他終於看完了每個房間、也講得氣喘吁吁後，便禮貌地把他們送回了門口。
	「很高興有這個機會聊聊，」他說。「除了波德里奇之外，我已經好一陣子沒機會跟人閒扯了。」
	「或許你不該一直把自己鎖在籠子裡，」@4說道。「你雖然擋住了可能的敵人，但也擋住了可能的盟友。」
	「這我想過，」他承認道。「只是眼下羅姆尼這一團亂實在讓人頭疼。我會好好考慮的。不管怎樣，你們幾位隨時歡迎回來坐坐。小心別讓人把你們給剝了皮！」�

entries.source:
The meeting hall was full.
	Assembled in the room were a dozen grizzled looking men, all seated around a long table at the head of which sat a young man sporting a goatee. As they entered, a servant quickly pointed them to a bench off to the side, indicating that a meeting of some import was underway.
	"...I don't care what Mitchel Waylander may or may not be doing," the bearded man said sternly. "óI am the Duke of Romney and you will do as I request, else I will call up others from Bas-Tyra. Do you really wish to call King Lyam's attention to this matter?"
	Unsettled by the vigor with which the young Duke made his point, the various guild leaders shifted in their seats. One, a tremendously overweight man whose clothes tested their seams, leaned forward, careful not to spark too much of a response. "It is entirely possible that the leader of the Riverpullers was assassinated by the leader of one of the other guilds here. It's even possible he sits in this room with us..."
	"If you have someone in mind, Botho, why don't you simply come out with a name!" another man replied, leaning across the table to grab the obese guild master's shirt. "Talk, you overweight cat's innard!"
	"Enough!" Slamming down the tankard of ale which sat at his right hand, the Duke turned his piercing blue eyes on all who assembled. "I want peace on the Romney, and I wish it today! The fact that the Ironmonger's Guild will not come to a negotiations table is irrelevant. If I hear another word of a possible uprising in Romney, I swear to you, I shall make each and every one of you pay for it..."
	Having heard enough of the heated words in the chamber, @4 turned and whispered to his companions. "If Arutha were here, he'd have this lot at the gibbet for even thinking of open rebellion..."
	"The fact of the matter is that Prince Arutha is ónot here," the Duke replied tersely, evidently having overheard the whispering. "And I will not deal so cavalierly with those who are as much my family as my serfs."
	Snapping his fingers, he motioned to a pair of guards who stood mute behind him. "Sergeant Yearly, see to it that these gentlemen are let out, seeing as how they yearn to get to a part of the world where Prince Arutha rules..."�
entries.translation:
會議廳裡擠滿了人。
	室內聚集著十來個滿面風霜的男人，全都圍坐在一張長桌旁，桌首坐著一個留著山羊鬍的年輕人。他們一進門，一名僕人便迅速指引他們坐到旁邊的一張長凳上，示意此刻正在進行一場要事會議。
	「……我才不管米契爾威蘭德到底在幹什麼還是沒幹什麼，」那個蓄鬍的男人語氣嚴厲地說道。「ó我是羅姆尼公爵，你們得照我的要求去做，不然我就從巴斯泰拉調人過來。你們真想引起萊亞姆王對這件事的注意嗎？」
	被這位年輕公爵語氣中的強硬鎮住，在座的幾位公會首領都不安地在座位上挪動著身子。其中一人，體型異常肥胖，衣服的接縫都繃得吃緊，他小心翼翼地向前傾身，生怕引來太多反應。「拉船工會的首領完全有可能是被這裡其他公會的首領派人暗殺的。他甚至可能就坐在我們這房間裡……」
	「波索，你要是心裡有數，何不乾脆說出個名字來！」另一個男人回道，探身越過桌子一把揪住這位肥胖公會會長的衣領。「說話啊，你這隻過胖的貓內臟！」
	「夠了！」公爵重重放下右手邊的麥酒杯，把那雙銳利的藍眼睛掃向在座眾人。「我要的是羅姆尼的和平，而且我今天就要！鐵匠公會不肯坐上談判桌根本不是理由。要是我再聽到有人說羅姆尼可能發生叛亂，我向你們發誓，我會讓你們每個人都付出代價……」
	聽夠了廳裡這番激烈的言辭，@4轉身低聲對同伴說道：「要是亞魯莎在這裡，光是有人動了公然叛亂的念頭，他就會把這幫人送上絞架了……」
	「事實是，亞魯莎親王ó不在這裡，」公爵語氣冷淡地回答道，顯然聽見了他的低語。「而我對待那些跟我農奴一樣算是我家人的人，可不會這麼隨便。」
	他打了個響指，示意站在身後一言不發的兩名守衛。「伊爾利軍士，把這幾位先生送出去，既然他們這麼渴望到亞魯莎親王管轄的地方去……」�

entries.source:
They were shown into a room.
	Seated cross legged in a large wooden chair, Duke Romney was staring at a large lumpy form which was heaped on top of the meeting table, his youngish features obviously clouded by some issue of great concern.
	"What's under the sheet?" @4 asked.
	"Botho Chandler," the Duke replied grimly. "They found him in the alleyway and have dropped him off here until the undertakers can come for him."
	"Murdered?"
	The Duke sighed. "Fortunately it's no great mystery. He was fighting with the leader of the Miller's Guild and got cornered by three mercenaries. We have them all in custody. Things have gotten so bad here that we're regularly building a bonfire to burn the bodies from this idiot private war between the Guilds."
	"Any way we can be of assistance?" @4 asked, taking a glance beneath the sheet at the obese corpse. "We may be in the area for some while."
	Drumming his fingers on the table, the Duke stared intently at them. "Actually, you may be of service to me," he said after a thoughtful moment. "If I can convince Arlie Steelsoul to come into negotiations with the rest of the guilds, it's possible I can break this deadlock between them. My father always said that the guilds will follow Mitchel Waylander and Arlie Steelsoul whichever way they go, but unfortunately Mitchel is too intertwined in the origins of this problem for me to use him effectively."
	"Where do we fit into this?" @4 asked.
	"You're neutral," he replied, gaining his feet. "You were born outside of Romney and you have no connections to the guilds...I am right about that aren't I?" Quickly an anxious look flickered in his eyes, but quickly vanished as he noticed that @4 was shaking his head. "Excellent. My point being, as the Duke, the guilds might view a private meeting between myself and Arlie as unfair negotiation. They have to believe that he is coming to the negotiation table of his own free will, and believe me, they will be watching my movements for a while."
	"So you want us to find this Arlie Steelsoul fellow and convince him to come and negotiate with the rest of the guilds, is that it?" @4 asked.
	"Just so," the Duke replied. "You will find that he has a small house to the west and south of here. I would advise you though, he is a paranoid man. He keeps himself well guarded and there may be some danger involved. I will reward you for your efforts of course."
	"That's all right," @4 said with a smile, heading towards the door. "We're used to danger."�
entries.translation:
他們被帶進了一間房間。
	羅姆尼公爵盤腿坐在一張大木椅上，盯著堆在會議桌上的一具龐大隆起的物體，他那張略顯年輕的臉龐上明顯籠罩著某種深切的憂慮。
	「布單底下是什麼？」@4問道。
	「波索錢德勒，」公爵沉重地回答道。「他們在巷子裡發現他的屍體，先丟在這裡，等殯葬業者來收。」
	「被謀殺的？」
	公爵嘆了口氣。「幸好這不是什麼大謎團。他跟磨坊工會的首領起了衝突，被三個傭兵逼到了角落裡。我們已經把他們全都收押了。事情鬧成這樣，我們現在得經常生火燒屍體，就為了平息公會之間這場愚蠢的私戰。」
	「有什麼我們能幫得上忙的嗎？」@4問道，順便瞄了一眼布單底下那具肥胖的屍體。「我們大概還會在這一帶待上一陣子。」
	公爵在桌上敲著手指，目不轉睛地盯著他們。「其實，你們或許幫得上我的忙，」他沉思片刻後說道。「要是我能說服亞利鋼魂坐上跟其他公會談判的桌子，或許就能打破他們之間的僵局。我父親生前總說，不管走哪條路，各公會都會跟著米契爾威蘭德跟亞利鋼魂走，可惜米契爾跟這場亂子的根源牽扯太深，我用不上他。」
	「這事跟我們有什麼關係？」@4問道。
	「你們是中立的，」他站起身回答道。「你們生在羅姆尼之外，跟這些公會毫無瓜葛……我這麼說沒錯吧？」他眼中閃過一絲焦慮，但很快就消失了，因為他注意到@4正在搖頭。「太好了。我的意思是，身為公爵，這些公會可能會把我跟亞利之間的私下會面看成不公平的協商。他們得相信他是自願來談判桌上的，而且，跟你們說實話，這段時間他們會一直盯著我的一舉一動。」
	「所以你是要我們去找這位亞利鋼魂，說服他來跟其他公會談判，是這個意思嗎？」@4問道。
	「正是如此，」公爵回答道。「你們會發現他家就在這裡的西南方，是間小屋。不過我得提醒你們，他是個疑心很重的人。他把自己防守得很嚴密，可能會有些危險。當然，我會酬謝你們的辛勞。」
	「沒關係，」@4微笑著說道，朝門口走去。「我們早就習慣危險了。」�

entries.source:
The Duke was surprised to see them.
	"Have you spoken with Arlie?" he asked. "Will he be coming back to negotiate?"
	"Haven't gotten through to him as yet," @4 said, looking around the room. "We've had a few other things to attend to."
	Immediately the Duke's eyes registered offense at @4's offhand comment, but quickly the seigneur recouped. "We are here at the request of Prince Arutha, Lord. I in no way intended to indicate that your problems here were secondary. We will attend to your affairs as soon as we may."
	Taking the Duke's glare as a cue it was time they got about their business, @4 quickly led them back into the streets of Romney...�
entries.translation:
公爵見到他們，有些意外。
	「你們跟亞利談過了嗎？」他問道。「他願意回來談判嗎？」
	「還沒能跟他搭上話，」@4環顧著房間說道。「我們還有其他幾件事要處理。」
	公爵的眼神頓時對@4這隨口的回答流露出些許不悅，但這位紳爵很快便補救了回來。「大人，我們是奉亞魯莎親王之命前來的。我絕無意暗示您這裡的事務是次要的。我們會盡快處理您的事。」
	把公爵這道銳利的目光當成了該辦正事的信號，@4很快便領著眾人回到了羅姆尼的街道上……�

entries.source:
The sergeant at arms halted them.
	Putting his hand against @4's chest, he shook his head. "I'm sorry, but the Duke is...". Abruptly he halted as the Duke appeared behind him.
	"It's all right," the Duke said. "Let them in, sergeant. I'm expecting these fellows. I'm expecting they've come to tell me they've convinced Arlie Steelsoul to come and help me out. Am I right?"
	@4 confirmed the fact quickly, following the Duke into the deserted meeting hall. Seeing the benches had been removed from the room, he seated himself unceremoniously on the table edge while @5 and @3 stood by the door.
	"Before I forget, your reward," the Duke said, opening a chest in the corner of the room. Sorting through what looked like torn table linens and soiled riding clothes, he at last found a pouch and tossed it to @4. Inside were several gold coins and a very valuable key. "I keep my promises," he said. "Now let's hope that Arlie does as well."
	"I don't see why he wouldn't," @4 said, packing away the Duke's gift. "He seemed honorable enough."
	"He's in charge of a Guild," the Duke replied. "He óhas to sound honorable. In their own way, the Guilds are more powerful than princedoms. You mark my words. One day the enfeoffed of the Kingdom will cross swords with the Guilds and it is not likely to be a bloodless affair. I think what's happened here is just a small taste of the things to come."
	"Glum words," @4 replied. "Do you think there will be more trouble here?"
	"Not for now. They've had enough of anarchy to do them a while and Arlie's coming to negotiations should settle things a bit."
	After chatting a while longer, @4 glanced up at the darkening windows. "It's getting late and we have other business to attend to."
	"Thank you for your services, gentlemen," the Duke said, escorting them to the door. "If you are ever in Romney again, please feel free to drop by and visit again."�
entries.translation:
武裝守衛的軍士攔下了他們。
	他伸手按在@4胸前，搖了搖頭。「很抱歉，但公爵正在……」他話說到一半突然停住，因為公爵已經出現在他身後。
	「沒關係，」公爵說道。「讓他們進來，軍士。我正等著這幾位先生。我猜他們是來告訴我，已經說服亞利鋼魂願意來幫我了。我猜得沒錯吧？」
	@4很快確認了這件事，跟著公爵走進了空無一人的會議廳。他見長凳已經從室內撤走，便毫不客氣地在桌邊坐下，@5與@3則站在門邊。
	「趁我還沒忘記，先給你們的酬勞，」公爵說道，打開了房間角落的一只箱子。他翻找著裡頭看似撕破的桌布與髒污的騎裝，終於找到一個錢袋，扔給了@4。裡頭裝著幾枚金幣與一把相當珍貴的鑰匙。「我向來說到做到，」他說。「現在但願亞利也是如此。」
	「我看不出他有什麼理由不這麼做，」@4收好公爵的贈禮，說道。「他看起來還算是個講信用的人。」
	「他掌管著一個公會，」公爵回答道。「他ó就得表現得講信用。就他們自己的方式來說，公會的權力甚至比諸侯還大。記住我這句話。總有一天，王國的封臣們會跟各大公會兵戎相見，而那場衝突恐怕不會兵不血刃。我想，這裡發生的這些事，不過是未來即將到來事態的一點縮影而已。」
	「聽起來真讓人沮喪，」@4回答道。「你覺得這裡還會有更多麻煩嗎？」
	「暫時不會了。他們這場無政府亂局也鬧夠了，亞利願意來談判，情勢應該能穩定一些。」
	又聊了一會兒，@4瞥了眼窗外漸暗的天色。「時候不早了，我們還有別的事要處理。」
	「感謝你們的幫忙，各位，」公爵說道，送他們到門口。「要是你們以後再來羅姆尼，請務必再來坐坐。」�

entries.source:
Duke Romney greeted them.
	"I hadn't counted on seeing you so soon again," he said. "Is all well with you?"
	"Fine," @4 said. "Actually, we were just passing through."
	Making a sound of acknowledgement, the Duke shrugged apologetically. "I should like to chat, but I've gotten word I am to send men to muster in Kenting Rush and I have many things to attend to. Perhaps another time."
	Accepting the Duke's apologies, they turned back from the meeting hall and into Romney's deserted streets.�
entries.translation:
羅姆尼公爵向他們打了招呼。
	「沒想到這麼快又見到你們了，」他說道。「你們一切都還好嗎？」
	「挺好的，」@4說。「其實我們只是路過而已。」
	公爵發出一聲了然的聲響，帶著歉意聳了聳肩。「我是很想跟你們聊聊，但我剛收到消息，得派人去肯廷拉什集結，還有很多事要處理。改天再說吧。」
	接受了公爵的致歉後，他們轉身離開了會議廳，走進了羅姆尼冷清的街道。�

entries.source:
@4 could smell alcohol.
	Pushing the door of the shop open, he was met by a sharp faced fellow who was carrying a wooden keg. Quickly dumping it with a pile of other casks, he wiped his hands off on a towel, then extended his hand.
	"Harlan," he said. "I'm the brew master around here when I'm not hauling things about."
	"And where exactly óis here?" @4 replied.
	"This is the Upturned Keg. We're the best brewery this side of the Romney. Would you care to sample some of our stock? We make a dandy apple wine," the proprietor said. "I can have some decanted for you."
	Refusing as politely as he knew how, @4 shook his head. "We have to keep our heads about us," he said. "We've a long road ahead and there's been some trouble around, or so I hear. We'll leave you to get back to your business."�

Harlan met them at the door.
	"Yes?" the brewer asked, his face smeared with a seedy looking grime.
	"We just thought we would pop in for a visit," @3 interjected. "If you weren't busy."
	"Don't have the time," the man said, wagging his head. "I'm working on a new batch and it needs constant attention. Sorry. Come back again some time."�
entries.translation:
哈蘭在門口迎接了他們。
	「有事嗎？」這位釀酒師問道，臉上沾滿了看起來髒兮兮的煙灰。
	「我們只是想順道進來看看，」@3插話道。「要是你不忙的話。」
	「沒空，」那男人說著，搖了搖頭。「我正在釀一批新酒，得隨時盯著才行。抱歉了。改天再來吧。」�

entries.source:
@4 could smell alcohol.
	Pushing the door of the shop open, he was met by a sharp faced fellow who was carrying a wooden keg. Quickly dumping it with a pile of other casks, he wiped his hands off on a towel, then extended his hand. "Welcome to the Upturned Keg. Best brewery this side of the Romney. Would you care to sample some of our stock? We make a dandy apple wine..."
	"I'm sure you do, but no thank you," @4 said. "We have other business with you. Have you recently sent a special delivery to the Black Sheep Tavern in Romney?"
	The man nodded. "Yes. A man here in town named Mitchel Waylander came in and made the purchase order himself. Paid with rubies."
	Recognizing the name of the leader of the Glazer's Guild of Romney, @4 arched an eyebrow. "Was there anything unusual about the order?"
	"I'll say," the man replied. Moving to a small bin, he pulled out a handful of a substance that looked like tabac, letting it sift between his fingers back into the bin. "He asked that I add this to the kegs---called black tarweed."
	"A poison?" @4 asked.
	"No. It's a cheat used by the less scrupulous tavern keepers. Handful of this dissolved in your ale, and whoever drinks it will think they're dying of thirst. Gets worse the more you drink."
	@5 spat. "It is often done in the north," he said. "A man will drink until he is no longer capable, either for lack of gold or wit."
	"And an excellent way to make certain that someone is incapable of fighting you back," @4 said with disgust. "The Nighthawks aren't what they used to be."
	Alarmed, the brew master seemed to pale. "Nighthawks? What have they to do with this?"
	Omitting most of the smaller details, @4 told what they had already learned of the murder. Horrified, the man shook his head. "I assure you, this has never once happened in association with the Keg. If you would like, I will get you something to drink. I guarantee that it has ónot been laced with the black tarweed..."�
entries.translation:
@4聞到了酒味。
	推開店門，一個尖臉男人扛著一只木桶迎面而來。他迅速把桶子跟其他木桶堆在一起，用毛巾擦了擦手，隨後伸出手。「歡迎光臨倒扣木桶酒館。羅姆尼這一帶最好的釀酒坊。要不要嚐嚐我們的酒？我們釀的蘋果酒可是一絕……」
	「我相信一定很棒，但不用了，謝謝，」@4說。「我們是有別的事找你。你最近有沒有送過一批特別的貨到羅姆尼的黑羊酒館？」
	那男人點了點頭。「有的。鎮上一個叫米契爾威蘭德的人親自過來下的訂單，用紅寶石付的錢。」
	認出這是羅姆尼玻璃匠公會會長的名字，@4挑了挑眉。「這筆訂單有什麼異常的地方嗎？」
	「這麼說吧，」那男人回答道。他走向一個小箱子，抓出一把看起來像菸草的東西，讓它從指縫間篩回箱子裡。「他要求我在酒桶裡加這個——叫黑焦草。」
	「毒藥？」@4問道。
	「不是。這是那些沒什麼良心的客棧老闆用來作弊的手段。往麥酒裡撒一把，誰喝了都會覺得自己渴得要命，快渴死了一樣。喝得越多就越嚴重。」
	@5啐了一口。「北境常有人這麼幹，」他說。「有人會一直喝，喝到再也沒法動彈為止，要嘛是沒錢了，要嘛是沒了理智。」
	「而且是個絕佳的手法，能確保對方沒法還手反擊，」@4厭惡地說道。「夜鷹會已經今非昔比了。」
	這位釀酒師傅聽得臉色發白，一臉驚慌。「夜鷹會？這跟他們有什麼關係？」
	略過大部分細節，@4把他們目前所知的謀殺案經過告訴了他。那男人聽了大驚失色，搖了搖頭。「我向你們保證，這種事在我們桶酒館從沒發生過。要是你們願意，我可以請你們喝一杯。我保證ó絕對沒摻黑焦草……」�

@4 knocked on the door.
	After a few moments, a dough faced woman answered, keeping one arm braced behind the door in case her visitors were less than congenial.
	"What is it you want?" Although she clearly was addressing @4, her gaze danced nervously to the moredhel. "I've had enough run ins with strangers of late."
	"Were we looking to get a bit of water per...," @4 started, but found the old woman had slammed the door.�
entries.translation:
@4敲了敲門。
	過了片刻，一個臉色蒼白的婦人應了門，一隻手臂始終撐在門後，以防來客不懷好意。
	「你們想幹嘛？」她顯然是在對@4說話，眼神卻不安地飄向那位莫瑞德人。「我最近跟陌生人打交道的次數已經夠多了。」
	「我們只是想要點水……」@4才開口，卻發現這位老婦人已經砰地一聲關上了門。�

entries.source:
Petrumh opened the door.
	Surprisingly alert for an elderly lady who had made a trek from Malac's Cross to Darkmoor unescorted, she greeted them with a broken toothed smile and motioned for them to come in. Shaking his head, @4 remained rooted in the doorway.
	"Sorry, we don't really have the time to come in," he apologized. "We just wanted to check in and see that you made your trip safely."
	"Oh, aye," she replied in her thick burr. "That I did. And what of you fellows? Did you by chance get back me cask I left at the Queen's Row?"�
entries.translation:
佩特魯姆開了門。
	這位獨自從馬拉克十字鎮徒步跋涉到黑沼鎮的老婦人，精神好得出乎意料，她露出缺了牙的笑容招呼他們，示意請他們進屋。@4搖了搖頭，仍站在門口沒動。
	「抱歉，我們其實沒什麼時間進去坐，」他致歉道。「我們只是想順道來看看，確認你一路平安到家了。」
	「哦，是啊，」她用濃重的鄉音回答道。「是平安到家了。那你們幾位呢？有沒有順道幫我把我留在王后巷旅店的那只木桶帶回來？」�

entries.source:
"That we did," @4 said, giving @5 a meaningful glance as he handed over the cask. "Just where you left it."
	"A better lad I couldn't hope for," she gushed, taking the cask. Once she had set it inside next to the door, she put her fingers to her mouth and whistled. "óOy, Ulam, where did you put those things I told you?"
	From the back of the house they could hear another woman's voice replying, though they couldn't exactly hear what was said. Nodding, Petrumh told them to wait a moment longer, disappearing inside the darkened interior.
	"Here they is," she said, reappearing after a few moments. With a quick motion she shoved a few trinkets into @4's hand. "Nothing all that special really, but you keep 'em. All right?"
	Again, the voice from the back of the house rose, but this time the words were faintly discernible. "ã.ã.ã.ãaãnãdã ãdãoãnã'ãtã ãyãoãuã ãlãeãtã ã'ãeãmã ãiãnã ãtãhãeã ã'ãoãuãsãeã,ã ãPãeãtã!ã ãSãtãrãaãnãgãeãrãsã ãaãrãeã ãnãoãtãhãiãnãgã ãbãuãtã ãtãrãoãuãbãlãeã.ã.ã."
	Rolling her eyes, Petrumh sighed apologetically. "Sorry, I've got to go, afore Ulam a'lays a cow. Thanks again, gents!"�
entries.translation:
「帶回來了，」@4說道，一邊把木桶遞了過去，一邊意味深長地看了@5一眼。「就放在你原本放的地方。」
	「我可找不到比你更好的小夥子了，」她欣喜地說道，接過木桶。她把桶子放進門邊後，把手指放進嘴裡吹了聲口哨。「ó喂，烏蘭，我叫你放的那些東西你放哪去了？」
	從屋子後方傳來另一個女人的回話聲，雖然聽不太清楚她在說什麼。佩特魯姆點了點頭，叫他們再稍等一下，隨後便消失在昏暗的屋內。
	「找到了，」她說著，過了片刻又出現在門口。她迅速把幾件小飾品塞進了@4手裡。「其實也沒什麼特別的，但你們留著吧，好嗎？」
	屋子後方那個聲音再次響起，這回，話語聲隱約能聽清楚了。「ã.ã.ã.ãaãnãdã ãdãoãnã'ãtã ãyãoãuã ãlãeãtã ã'ãeãmã ãiãnã ãtãhãeã ã'ãoãuãsãeã,ã ãPãeãtã!ã ãSãtãrãaãnãgãeãrãsã ãaãrãeã ãnãoãtãhãiãnãgã ãbãuãtã ãtãrãoãuãbãlãeã.ã.ã.」
	佩特魯姆翻了個白眼，帶著歉意嘆了口氣。「抱歉，我得走了，免得烏蘭又要嘮叨個沒完。再次謝謝你們了，兩位！」�
